sentences.text: Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch has announced she will overhaul inheritance tax if her party wins the next general election.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: She told the Conservatives' annual conference that "nobody will ever pay inheritance tax on their family home" and couples will be able to leave an additional £1m tax free.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: Tax experts say the party's £6bn per year estimate of the cost of the plan is reasonable, but warn the policy would primarily benefit wealthier households and could discourage older people from moving to smaller homes.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: BBC Verify has looked into the details of the policy.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: Under the current system, inheritance tax of 40% is paid when someone's estate - the total value of their money and property - exceeds £325,000.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: Anything under this amount is not taxed.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: And, when a person dies, they can currently transfer this tax-free allowance to a surviving spouse or civil partner which increases the combined threshold for a couple to £650,000.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: On top of this individuals can get an additional transferable allowance for a family home of £175,000 each when it is left to children or other direct descendants.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: So at present most married couples can potentially leave £1m without paying inheritance tax.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: The Conservative plan would increase the £325,000 threshold - the point at which you start paying the tax - to £500,000 and fully exempt a family home from inheritance tax.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: At the moment an estate with a £2m house could be liable for £400,000 in inheritance tax.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: That would reduce to zero under the Conservatives.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: Official figures show that in 2024-25 around 30,400 deaths in the UK left estates which were liable for inheritance tax.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: This was around 5% of all UK deaths in that year.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: But the number of estates paying inheritance tax is set to rise, due to the increasing value of inherited wealth being passed on and the threshold having been frozen.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: The Institute for Fiscal Studies (IFS) has estimated that by 2032-33 around 12% of people will have inheritance tax due either on their own death or that of their spouse or civil partner.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: Citing analysis by the consultancy Oxford Economics, the Conservatives say the number of estates paying the tax will rise to 52,100 in 2029-30.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: The Conservatives estimate their reforms would reduce the number of affected estates in 2030 to 22,000.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: Official data shows higher value estates pay the majority of the inheritance tax collected.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: The IFS has estimated that if inheritance tax were to be entirely scrapped, which Badenoch has identified as a longer term aspiration, the wealthiest 1% of estates - those worth £2.1m or more - would get half of the benefit of the tax reduction.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: And one long-standing criticism of inheritance tax is that the wealthy use legal ways to avoid paying it like putting their assets into family trusts to reduce the amount of inheritance tax ultimately due from their estates when they die.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: In 2023-24, estates with a valuation of £10m only paid an average effective inheritance tax rate of 18%, according to estimates from HM Revenue and Customs.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: Responding to Wednesday's conference announcement, the IFS said: "The biggest beneficiaries would be those with the highest wealth and the most valuable homes – and their descendants.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: "This is a very well-off group, mainly living in London and the South-East of England." The Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR), the official forecaster, estimates inheritance tax will raise £9.5bn in 2026-27 - equivalent to around 0.3% of GDP.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: The OBR projects this will rise to £14.5bn in 2030-31 or 0.4% of GDP.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: The Conservatives estimate their plan would cost £6bn a year in 2029-30, based on Oxford Economics' analysis.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: The party says it has identified £71bn in annual savings including £36bn a year from welfare cuts.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: Prof Andy Summers, director of the Centre for the Analysis of Taxation, told BBC Verify this was "just about about the worst possible way to deliver an inheritance tax cut".
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: "Exempting the family home however much it's worth will just encourage older people to concentrate their savings in their home, prevent downsizing, and so further gum up the housing market," he said.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: The Conservatives argue in their press release accompanying the policy announcement that inheritance taxes are "bad for growth".
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.text: But analysis by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development suggests inheritance taxes in general are less damaging to economic growth than taxes on income from work.
sentences.article_title: What's in the Conservatives' inheritance tax plan and who benefits?

sentences.article_title: Western civilisation at risk of 'atrophy, servitude and decline', Rubio says

sentences.article_title: Western civilisation at risk of 'atrophy, servitude and decline', Rubio says

sentences.text: "We believe that Europe can awaken from its long slumber and rekindle the fire that was here millennia ago," he said.
sentences.article_title: Western civilisation at risk of 'atrophy, servitude and decline', Rubio says

sentences.article_title: Western civilisation at risk of 'atrophy, servitude and decline', Rubio says

sentences.article_title: Western civilisation at risk of 'atrophy, servitude and decline', Rubio says

sentences.article_title: Western civilisation at risk of 'atrophy, servitude and decline', Rubio says

sentences.article_title: Western civilisation at risk of 'atrophy, servitude and decline', Rubio says

sentences.text: The winners are awarded the Nobel Prize medal and a share of 12.0 million Swedish Kroner ($1.25m; £900,000) The Nobel Prize in Chemistry has been awarded to French scientist Henri B.
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: Kagan and Japan's Kenso Soai for providing a solution to the chemical mystery of life's asymmetry.
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: The researchers discovered how nature exclusively makes the correct version of a molecule - rather than its mirror image.
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: For example, amino acid molecules, the building blocks of proteins, exist as two forms that are each other's mirror image.
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: But living organisms on Earth only function with one of those forms.
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: The Nobel laureates answered the question: why does life favour just one of these mirror image molecules over the other.
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: In organic chemistry, this property is known as "chirality", so chiral molecules have both right and left-handed forms.
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: You can think of them as looking like our hands - not identical, but each a mirror image of the other.
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: And while nature almost exclusively produces the version it requires to function, chemical reactions in a lab usually create a 50-50 mix of both left- and right-handed molecules.
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: When it comes to making drugs, this is particularly significant, because each version behaves differently when it interacts with our bodies.
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: So, one might have disease-fighting properties, while the other version does nothing or even causes harm.
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: The development of the Thalidomide drug is an example of this.
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: In the 1950s it was prescribed to pregnant women suffering with morning sickness.
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: But it is a chiral molecule - the right-handed version is an effective treatment, but the left-hand is toxic.
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: The original drug given was a mixture of the two, and it was later discovered that the body will convert between the two.
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: The result was thousands of children, born to women who took the drug, developed severe disabilities.
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: Heiner Linke, chair of the Nobel Committee for Chemistry, explained: "Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai have provided a solution to a chemical mystery that is over a century old: how homochirality - the selective production of the correct version of a molecule - can emerge spontaneously.
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: "The chemical reactions they have developed are spectacular." Henri Kagan, who is at Université Paris-Sud, first discovered a new way of manipulating chemical reactions in 1986.
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: This allowed him to create a greater excess of one of the mirror images than had previously been thought possible.
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: Kenso Soai from Tokyo University of Science took the next step in 1995.
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: He published a scientific paper in the journal Nature , external describing the first ever chemical reaction that had the potential to be homochiral - producing only the desired version of an organic molecule.
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: In 2003, he finally succeeded in controlling a reaction in which only one of the two possible mirror images was formed.
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: "Other than life itself," the Nobel Committee said in a statement, "no one had previously achieved this feat".
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: At the press conference on Wednesday, Kenso Soai praised the "many, many excellent researchers" in this field.
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: Professor Robert Mokaya, president of the UK's Royal Society of Chemistry said it was a "powerful example of how fundamental chemistry can underpin solutions to some of the biggest challenges facing society".
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: "Different isomers (or versions of molecules) can have completely different biological and physical effects, so they are crucial in finding effective medicines to treat all sorts of illnesses," he added.
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: Chirality is the foundation for animal features, like the way snail shells coil to the right Prof Angus Davison, from the University of Nottingham, studies the biology of chirality and said that the Nobel-winning chemistry could help reveal how and why life favours "one-handedness".
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: "In ways that we don't yet quite understand, the chirality of the basic building blocks of life ends up making bodies that are themselves also chiral," he told BBC News.
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: This was the foundation, he explained, of our hearts being on left hand side of our bodies and snail shells that coil to the right.
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: Peter Somfai, a member of the Nobel Committee for Chemistry, said the research awarded this year's prize has become part of "our basic understanding of how chemistry functions".
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: He said showing how a mirror image is created is "probably the most fundamental question in life - because somehow that happened four billion years ago when life was created.
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: And now we have, for the first time, mimicked that in the lab".
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: Ramon Vega made 23 appearances for Switzerland between 1993 and 2001 Former Tottenham Hotspur defender Ramon Vega says he intends to stand as a candidate in next year's Fifa presidential election.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Spurs player Vega set to run for Fifa president

sentences.text: The 55-year-old is the first person to confirm they want to challenge Gianni Infantino, who has defied calls to step down in the wake of his failed plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors, which has sparked a major backlash across football.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Spurs player Vega set to run for Fifa president

sentences.text: A former Switzerland centre-back, Vega also played for Celtic and Watford and has worked in finance since retiring from football in 2004.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Spurs player Vega set to run for Fifa president

sentences.text: "I am standing to reunite the global football family, deliver genuine and lasting reform, modernise Fifa for the 21st Century, restore stability and credibility, and rebuild the trust that our game urgently needs," he said.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Spurs player Vega set to run for Fifa president

sentences.text: Meanwhile, Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa - president of the Asian Football Confederation - has written to Infantino, distancing himself from an external review of Fifa's governance system.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Spurs player Vega set to run for Fifa president

sentences.text: In his letter - seen by BBC Sport - Sheikh Salman proposes that Fifa's council sets up a working group to examine potential reforms, "rather than being outsourced to an external party".
sentences.article_title: Ex-Spurs player Vega set to run for Fifa president

sentences.text: Last month, Infantino said he was "fully committed to leading Fifa" despite Uefa, Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation calling for him to quit.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Spurs player Vega set to run for Fifa president

sentences.text: Vega considered running for Fifa's top job in 2015 following the suspension of former president Sepp Blatter.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Spurs player Vega set to run for Fifa president

sentences.text: Four years later he said he would stand against Infantino, but failed to garner enough support to be included in the ballot, having required the backing of five of Fifa's 211 member federations.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Spurs player Vega set to run for Fifa president

sentences.text: Candidates must also be proposed by a member association and played an active role in the game for two of the past five years, as well as passing an eligibility check by a review committee.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Spurs player Vega set to run for Fifa president

sentences.text: "I am standing because my life has prepared me to serve the game," Vega said in a statement announcing his candidacy.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Spurs player Vega set to run for Fifa president

sentences.text: "Football does not belong to presidents, confederations or administrators.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Spurs player Vega set to run for Fifa president

sentences.text: Football is greater than any position, any individual or any institution.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Spurs player Vega set to run for Fifa president

sentences.text: "It is the people's game and belongs to everyone: the players, coaches, referees, supporters, volunteers, clubs, leagues, associations and communities that give football its life.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Spurs player Vega set to run for Fifa president

sentences.text: "It belongs to every child discovering the game, every professional carrying the hopes of a nation, and the billions of supporters whose passion makes football the world's game.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Spurs player Vega set to run for Fifa president

sentences.text: "Football must always come first.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Spurs player Vega set to run for Fifa president

sentences.text: Yet for too long, division has fractured our football family.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Spurs player Vega set to run for Fifa president

sentences.text: "The current leadership has demoralised the game.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Spurs player Vega set to run for Fifa president

sentences.text: Weak governance has damaged Fifa's credibility and eroded trust across the global football family.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Spurs player Vega set to run for Fifa president

sentences.text: We must stop this conflict from escalating.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Spurs player Vega set to run for Fifa president

sentences.text: "Ego-driven battles within football administration must never be allowed to damage those who matter most: the players, coaches, referees and supporters around the world.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Spurs player Vega set to run for Fifa president

sentences.text: They are not responsible for these conflicts.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Spurs player Vega set to run for Fifa president

sentences.text: They deserve better." Vega concluded: "Football is in the emergency room, on life support.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Spurs player Vega set to run for Fifa president

sentences.text: We cannot wait any longer.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Spurs player Vega set to run for Fifa president

sentences.text: Fifa needs a new direction and fundamental reform.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Spurs player Vega set to run for Fifa president

sentences.text: "We must reunite the football family, restore trust, bring stability and modernise Fifa's governance.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Spurs player Vega set to run for Fifa president

sentences.text: At the time, the three confederations said any review of Fifa's governance must be "conducted by a fully independent third party".
sentences.article_title: Ex-Spurs player Vega set to run for Fifa president

sentences.text: Now, however, Salman says he believes the process should be "driven by the football institutions themselves, rather than being outsourced to an external party".
sentences.article_title: Ex-Spurs player Vega set to run for Fifa president

sentences.text: He added: "I believe there is value in taking this opportunity to consider constructively whether Fifa's existing governance arrangements can be strengthened.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Spurs player Vega set to run for Fifa president

sentences.text: "The issue is not necessarily whether this requires a wholesale redesign of Fifa's governance system." Fifa's council meets in Zurich next week for the first time since the FFE plan emerged in July.

sentences.text: Arsenal are chasing back-to-back Premier League titles Just five games in, it might seem a bit early to pay much attention to the Premier League table - but it's probably more settled than you think.

sentences.text: However, one part of the table that does not settle quickly is the top spot.

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: What the Paramount and Warner Bros deal means for you It has been months in the making but Paramount Skydance has finally completed its $110bn (£82.8bn) merger with Warner Bros Discovery.
sentences.article_title: From films to streaming prices - how the Warner Bros deal could affect you

sentences.text: The deal welds two legacy Hollywood powerhouses, uniting franchises like Harry Potter and Game of Thrones, into an entertainment behemoth named Skydance.
sentences.article_title: From films to streaming prices - how the Warner Bros deal could affect you

sentences.text: Yet behind this milestone lies strict rules about what the combined business can and cannot do - from how many films it must produce a year to the editorial independence of its newsroom.

sentences.text: Here are four ways this could affect you and the movies, TV and news you watch.
sentences.article_title: From films to streaming prices - how the Warner Bros deal could affect you

sentences.text: HBO Max is the company behind Euphoria, a series starring Zendaya Warner Bros owns HBO Max, home to The Sopranos, House of the Dragon and Euphoria among others.
sentences.article_title: From films to streaming prices - how the Warner Bros deal could affect you

sentences.text: Meanwhile, Paramount Skydance has Paramount+, which streams the likes of Yellowstone, Parks and Recreation and NCIS.
sentences.article_title: From films to streaming prices - how the Warner Bros deal could affect you

sentences.text: Combining HBO Max and Paramount+ into a single platform or bundle will likely squeeze subscribers' wallets over time.
sentences.article_title: From films to streaming prices - how the Warner Bros deal could affect you

sentences.text: While existing subscribers to both might enjoy short-term savings, analysts expect overall prices to rise as the combined giant seeks profitability .
sentences.article_title: From films to streaming prices - how the Warner Bros deal could affect you

sentences.text: The merged company, Skydance, carries a massive $80bn in debt from the deal, even as executives target $6bn in annual cost savings.
sentences.article_title: From films to streaming prices - how the Warner Bros deal could affect you

sentences.text: Analysts warn that consumers will ultimately bear the financial burden of the $110bn deal.
sentences.article_title: From films to streaming prices - how the Warner Bros deal could affect you

sentences.text: Mike Proulx, research director at Forrester, noted that with streaming services constantly raising fees to increase profitability and Skydance saddled with massive debt, price increases are likely to come.

sentences.text: While viewers will gain access to a broader catalogue, as Skydance shifts toward a Paramount+ and HBO Max bundle rather than a single app, Proulx warns that "it's far-fetched to think it'll prevent downstream price hikes".

sentences.text: Paramount and Warner Bros are coming together to form Skydance As part of a settlement deal with US states who had objected to the merger , Paramount Skydance has agreed to release a set number of films every year for the next five years.
sentences.article_title: From films to streaming prices - how the Warner Bros deal could affect you

sentences.text: For the first two years, that's 30 movies annually, and for the remaining period it has to release 32 films each year.
sentences.article_title: From films to streaming prices - how the Warner Bros deal could affect you

sentences.article_title: From films to streaming prices - how the Warner Bros deal could affect you

sentences.text: The merged studio must also release at least four independent films each year.
sentences.article_title: From films to streaming prices - how the Warner Bros deal could affect you

sentences.text: If Skydance misses its movie quota, it could be forced to sell its 49% stake in Miramax – the studio co-founded by disgraced Hollywood mogul Harvey Weinstein.
sentences.article_title: From films to streaming prices - how the Warner Bros deal could affect you

sentences.article_title: From films to streaming prices - how the Warner Bros deal could affect you

sentences.text: "Once those obligations expire, the company will have far more flexibility," she said.
sentences.article_title: From films to streaming prices - how the Warner Bros deal could affect you

sentences.text: "Temporary rules cannot permanently fix a structural market shift".
sentences.article_title: From films to streaming prices - how the Warner Bros deal could affect you

sentences.text: Once the five-year deal ends, Skydance could follow rivals like Disney and Netflix by prioritizing streaming over cinema.
sentences.article_title: From films to streaming prices - how the Warner Bros deal could affect you

sentences.text: As Disney's $71bn buyout of 21st Century Fox in 2019 proved, mega-deals can lead to fewer films in cinemas.
sentences.article_title: From films to streaming prices - how the Warner Bros deal could affect you

sentences.article_title: From films to streaming prices - how the Warner Bros deal could affect you

sentences.text: Royal Mail said posties are protected from the proposed cuts Royal Mail has announced plans to cut 2,500 head office and other supporting roles by the end of 2027 as it battles competition and falling demand for letter deliveries.

sentences.text: Rainmaker's drones were used over Alaska this year On 23 August, Cooper Freeman had no idea clouds above his head were being filled with a silver compound in order to cause rainfall.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Neither did thousands of other residents in Homer, Alaska, who later discovered San Francisco start-up Rainmaker conducted an experiment in that region using cloud-seeding technology.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: The company claims it produced 19 million US gallons of water in the sky in three hours.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: This approach to weather modification, now more than 80-years-old, involves using planes and drones to disperse compounds such as silver iodide into clouds to form ice crystals.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Those crystals eventually become large enough to fall as rain or snow, depending on the temperatures below.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Essentially, cloud seeding speeds up the natural process of water vapor condensing inside of clouds.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Gravity then pulls those crystals to the ground.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: The technology, though, needs ideal climate environments, such as mountainous or cold regions such as Alaska.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Freeman, the Alaska director of the Center for Biological Diversity, isn't just concerned Homer residents weren't widely alerted to these experiments.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: He's sceptical about what was shot into the clouds, and questions how safe it was for both residents and their habitat.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: "It doesn't appear that there was any downstream monitoring to verify that this silver iodide didn't impact the environment," he says.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Freeman adds, "Having a company come in to do this seeding isn't going to solve our water woes, and it feels like a distraction from solving the urgent issues related to water conservation." Concerns are mounting about the challenges surrounding water security.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres said in July "our world is using freshwater faster than it can be replenished , external ", which echoes reports noting how the past five years have led to the driest period for global rivers , external in more than three decades.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Cloud-seeding technology may be a drop in the bucket, as it doesn't create rainstorms.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: For example, Rainmaker's 19 million gallons equates to around 0.01 inch of rain across 100 square miles.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Nevertheless, more than 50 countries , external are developing programmes to modify the weather and a surge of start-ups are developing systems to create rain.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: As well developed and promising as this innovative field has become, these businesses continue to face thorny questions on safety and efficacy, leading to novel approaches with both finding the right material to spray into clouds and how they do it.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Augustus Doricko with a Rainmaker drone Augustus Doricko, the founder and CEO of Rainmaker, is quick to answer any questions on the consequences of how his company uses the silver iodide compound.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: It's clear he's been asked about chemical safety many times.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: He says Rainmaker releases this form of silver at 20 grams per flight, distributed across thousands of square kilometres.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Cloud-seeding sessions have to wait for clouds to form to try to coax them into precipitation.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Their drones are outfitted with silver iodide flairs, and when lit the burning atomizes the water particles into a small enough size so they can stay suspended in the freezing cloud for hours, eventually turning into crystals and later rain.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Rainmaker operates in states such as Idaho, Utah, Colorado and areas of the Middle East such as Jordan.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: A year later, silver iodide was found to be more effective than dry ice, which quickly turns into useless gas.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: While seeding agents caused more rainfall, they didn't move the needle much.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: In fact, sobering statistics point to how patchy this technology can be in what it pours on the ground.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: "With the right conditions, cloud seeding squeeze out about an extra five to 10% of precipitation," says Jon Meyer, an assistant state climatologist with the Utah Climate Center.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: What was encouraging, though, for the cloud-seeding sector was a landmark 2017 study that found how silver iodide worked as expected, one of the first reports to observe cloud seeding in action using radar and precipitation gauges.

sentences.text: In the past several years, Meyer has been encouraged to see more companies such as Rainmaker bring innovation to an old industry.

Olivia Li is developing an alternative to silver iodide for cloud seeding What is sprayed into clouds may also be undergoing a major shift.

sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: For ten years, Jonathan Blow has been working with a small team on what he believes is "the biggest puzzle game ever made".

sentences.text: The American developer is renowned as one of the fathers of the modern indie game movement, creating the genre-defining puzzle-platformer Braid in 2008.
sentences.article_title: Braid-creator Jonathan Blow on making the 'biggest puzzle game ever'

sentences.text: Now, a decade on from his last project, The Witness, The Order of the Sinking Star is due to be released on Thursday - a game with roughly 1,500 puzzles that he estimates could take around 500 hours to complete.
sentences.article_title: Braid-creator Jonathan Blow on making the 'biggest puzzle game ever'

sentences.text: So why make something the majority of players may never get even halfway through, let alone finish?

sentences.text: "Some people decide what to make based on what's practical or what makes business sense," Blow says.
sentences.article_title: Braid-creator Jonathan Blow on making the 'biggest puzzle game ever'

sentences.text: "It's never been the way that I think." "I sort of make bad business decisions in a sense...because I let the design dominate that process.
sentences.article_title: Braid-creator Jonathan Blow on making the 'biggest puzzle game ever'

sentences.text: But then because we did that, we always have something unique," he says.
sentences.article_title: Braid-creator Jonathan Blow on making the 'biggest puzzle game ever'

sentences.text: The blurb of the game - releasing on PC, Nintendo Switch 2, and PlayStation 5 - likens itself to a "game design supercollider".
sentences.article_title: Braid-creator Jonathan Blow on making the 'biggest puzzle game ever'

sentences.text: The player travels through four worlds, viewed from overhead, which are built on the mechanics of four pre-existing free puzzle games from other designers (with their permission to do so).
sentences.article_title: Braid-creator Jonathan Blow on making the 'biggest puzzle game ever'

sentences.text: These ideas are then "smashed together" to create hundreds of brand-new brainteasers.
sentences.article_title: Braid-creator Jonathan Blow on making the 'biggest puzzle game ever'

sentences.text: For example, one world's mechanics, based on those from the free 2014 game Mirror Isles by Alan Hazelden, sees players use mirror reflections to swap places across islands.
sentences.article_title: Braid-creator Jonathan Blow on making the 'biggest puzzle game ever'

sentences.text: When combined with the system of another free game created by Hazelden, Skipping Stones to Lonely Homes - where players throw stones into water to create paths - brand-new puzzle opportunities suddenly arise.

sentences.article_title: Braid-creator Jonathan Blow on making the 'biggest puzzle game ever'

sentences.article_title: Braid-creator Jonathan Blow on making the 'biggest puzzle game ever'

sentences.text: Blow, who has not responded to these critiques publicly, tells me he instead decided to "sit down and focus on the games".

sentences.text: Starting in 2027, the agreement replaces a rotation of the gala among major networks like ABC, CBS, Fox and NBC.
sentences.article_title: Amazon wins global rights to stream Emmys in six-year deal

sentences.text: The ceremony will instead stream live for free worldwide each September, with no Prime Video subscription needed.
sentences.article_title: Amazon wins global rights to stream Emmys in six-year deal

sentences.text: Official terms were not disclosed.
sentences.article_title: Amazon wins global rights to stream Emmys in six-year deal

sentences.text: The BBC has contacted Amazon and the Emmys for comment.
sentences.article_title: Amazon wins global rights to stream Emmys in six-year deal

sentences.text: The move is another indication of how live events are shifting to digital platforms as viewing habits evolve.
sentences.article_title: Amazon wins global rights to stream Emmys in six-year deal

sentences.text: The Oscars, for example, are moving to YouTube live globally starting in 2029.
sentences.article_title: Amazon wins global rights to stream Emmys in six-year deal

sentences.text: Mike Proulx, research director at Forrester, said the existing setup had become out of sync with modern television.
sentences.article_title: Amazon wins global rights to stream Emmys in six-year deal

sentences.text: "The shows driving the industry forward largely originate on streaming platforms, yet the awards themselves were tethered to broadcast television," Proulx said.
sentences.article_title: Amazon wins global rights to stream Emmys in six-year deal

sentences.text: "That's why a leading streaming service like Prime Video makes sense for the Emmy's next act." Cris Abrego, chair of the Television Academy, said the deal gives the ceremony "unprecedented global reach", allowing audiences in more than 200 countries to watch live.
sentences.article_title: Amazon wins global rights to stream Emmys in six-year deal

sentences.text: "Television has never been more global, and the Emmys should be a celebration that the world can share," Abrego said in a statement issued by Amazon.
sentences.article_title: Amazon wins global rights to stream Emmys in six-year deal

sentences.article_title: Amazon wins global rights to stream Emmys in six-year deal

sentences.article_title: Amazon wins global rights to stream Emmys in six-year deal

sentences.article_title: Amazon wins global rights to stream Emmys in six-year deal

sentences.text: OpenAI chief strategy officer Jason Kwon faced a parliamentary hearing into AI in Sydney OpenAI has admitted its actions were "not good enough" after one of its rogue agents breached Australian government websites in June, saying it had added more precautions to its training environments.

sentences.text: The company's chief strategy officer Jason Kwon faced a parliamentary hearing into AI on Tuesday in Sydney, saying the breach "should not have happened" and it "should have handled our response better".
sentences.article_title: OpenAI admits response to Australian government hacks 'not good enough'

sentences.text: It took weeks before Australia was notified via an email to a generic inbox.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI admits response to Australian government hacks 'not good enough'

sentences.text: "We are sorry and we know we have work to do to rebuild trust with the Australian people," Kwon said.

sentences.text: Executives from Microsoft and Google were also present.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI admits response to Australian government hacks 'not good enough'

sentences.text: An OpenAI agent went "rogue" and "infiltrated" a private statistics portal containing "non-sensitive" data from Australia's universal healthcare scheme Medicare in June, in what cyber-security experts said was the first hack of its kind.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI admits response to Australian government hacks 'not good enough'

sentences.text: When asked why OpenAI had not directly contacted government ministers immediately after it found out about the breaches, Kwon acknowledged it was a mistake.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI admits response to Australian government hacks 'not good enough'

sentences.text: "In retrospect, we should have done what you're suggesting," Kwon said.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI admits response to Australian government hacks 'not good enough'

sentences.text: "The reason why it happened the way that it did is I think people were thinking about this as a technical situation and they wanted to contact the technical counterparties, but it's not good enough." Kwon said the company has changed how it handles such incidents.

sentences.text: The company was also establishing a local taskforce in Australia to investigate "how to better manage the risks associated with increasingly capable AI", it said.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI admits response to Australian government hacks 'not good enough'

sentences.text: Choosing the right moment to harvest can be a make-or-break decision When the first day of the apple harvest rolled around in Washington State last year, the fruit was ripe and the pickers were ready – but the weather had other ideas.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "It was like 38C… it's not safe for people to work in that heat," recalls Joel Carter at Okanagan Specialty Fruits.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "We had to stop at 10 o'clock in the morning." He says that artificial intelligence (AI) models that forecast ideal harvest dates, taking into account the weather, would be useful.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "You need to know more than just when your fruit is going to be ripe.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: How long do you have to pick it?" he says.

sentences.text: "That's where these models are really helpful." Carter's company has more than 1,250 acres of apple orchards in Washington, and the fruit is grown for sliced apple portions – often sold to hotels and schools, for example.

sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: The cameras are mounted atop tractors and they scoop up imagery of the apple trees as the tractor trundles by.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: AI identifies buds, flowers or fruit in that footage.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "Right now, Vivid is telling us crop estimates and harvest dates," says Carter.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: He notes that the system is good at picking out very tiny flower buds, which are hard to see at a glance with the naked eye.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: But the accuracy of forecasts is noticeably dependent on the quality of historical information fed in to the system, adds Carter.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "This isn't something where an AI can scrape the internet and figure out what's the average [yield] for Granny Smith," he explains.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "It's going to be bespoke to your farm." Apples are at least somewhat forgiving – the harvest window for those Granny Smiths is three weeks long, says Carter.

sentences.text: For other fruit, such as berries, you might only have a few days.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "If a strawberry crop is on, you have to harvest it – otherwise your entire crop gets diseased very, very quickly," says Raymond Martin, co-founder and chief operating officer of FruitCast, a UK company that offers harvest forecasts to fruit growers here.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: His firm offers growers crop predictions for strawberries and also raspberries, blackberries, blueberries and tomatoes.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "We're moving on to grapes next year," adds Martin.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Don't experienced farmers know when their fruit will be ripe, I ask?
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Martin says they generally do – but not necessarily across their entire farm, which might be many acres in size, or have both outdoor and indoor growing areas.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: This has stressed many fruit plants, putting them into thermal dormancy and slowing down fruit production.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: There's only a small window for picking berries says Raymond Martin The FruitCast model accounts for weather and irrigation conditions in its forecasts.

sentences.text: Europe's heatwave has boosted demand for battery storage systems As heatwaves scorched Europe this summer, workers at a US battery company noticed an uptick in demand.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: San Diego-based Unigrid sells a nine kilowatt hour battery for people's homes.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Sweltering European homeowners were apparently looking for ways of storing power when it was available from the grid at lower rates.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: They could then run air conditioners more cheaply, off the battery, during the worst heat of the day.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "We have requests coming from Spain, France, Germany, The Netherlands," says Darren Tan, co-founder and chief executive.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "We've shipped the first 100 units and [expect to ship] 1,000 before the end of the year." Unigrid's battery is an emerging technology – it's a sodium ion, rather than lithium ion device.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Sodium ion batteries have got energy storage experts excited because they could end up much cheaper to build and operate than lithium ion.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: They're potentially less likely to catch fire and should also work in a wider range of temperatures, even down to lows of minus 40C , external .
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Darren Tan founded Unigrid - a maker of sodium ion batteries But there's a debate over what constitutes the best, and safest, sodium ion battery design.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Plus, more than one , external US company working in this space has floundered in recent years , external .
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: China leads the world in sodium ion battery manufacturing at present so US competitors are going to have to work hard to keep up.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: The prize that awaits is the possibility of batteries made in the US with 100% US-sourced materials.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: This is unlike lithium ion batteries, where China dominates the materials , external supply chain as well as manufacturing.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: For Tan, China has helped his company get to market.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: The Unigrid battery currently uses sodium ion cells made there, rather than in the US.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "We can switch back and forth and choose what battery we want to work with," says Tan, explaining that, in future, his firm might source cells from the US – though these may come at a different cost.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: There's another consideration.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Unigrid's battery contains chromium-3 in its cathode.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: In a battery, electrons flow from cathode to anode , external when charging and in the opposite direction when discharging or providing power.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Ivana Hasa, at the Warwick Manufacturing Group, University of Warwick, who has no connection to Unigrid, agrees that it is possible for chromium-3 to form chromium-6 at very high states of charge, though she says this can be mitigated by how voltage is controlled within the battery.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "Safety tests reported on the cell chemistry are very promising," she says of Unigrid's tech.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Tan says concerns around toxicity of the battery's materials are "overblown" and emphasises that Unigrid's battery has passed certification and safety tests for sale in Europe and is currently undergoing such evaluations for the US market.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Third-party tests have not been able to get the battery to form chromium-6, he says.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "We've tried very hard to try and produce it, we've overcharged it as much as we can...
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: We were unsuccessful in generating chromium-6." The choice of cathode material, or how the electrolyte – which separates cathode and anode – is formulated are key details influencing the performance and longevity of sodium ion batteries.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Some manufacturers are not using chromium for their cathode but hard carbon instead, or sodium iron phosphate pyrophosphate (NFPP).
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: In general, confidence around sodium ion batteries' reliability has increased during the last few years, says Prof Dame Grey, meaning they are now finding their way into grid storage applications.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Last December, LFP batteries – a relatively cheap form of lithium ion battery – were trading at $81 per kilowatt hour , external (kWh) whereas Unigrid's sodium ion battery pricing is roughly $100 kWh , external .
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Some companies that spoke to the BBC suggested sodium ion might reach as low as $30 per kWh but analysts say significantly lower costs could be many years away , external .
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Sodium ion batteries are also not as energy dense as lithium ion batteries, meaning they must be slightly bigger and heavier in order to provide the same amount of power.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: The technology has been improving , external on this front in recent years but, even so, you're not likely to see sodium ion cells in small, energy hungry devices such as smartphones.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Larger energy storage solutions are where most people expect sodium ion to dominate.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: He points out that sodium ion batteries could help distribute renewable energy to data centres.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: The long nose of the X-59 is designed to dampen the plane's sonic boom There's a weird and wonderful jet flying over the US.

sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: On top of its bizarre appearance the X-59 boasts a remarkable lineage.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: It's the latest in a series of experimental Nasa aircraft dating back to 1947 and the first plane to break the sound barrier, the Bell X-1.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: Peter Coen, a 43-year Nasa veteran who manages the programme, explains the thinking behind 80 years of X-planes.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: "Our approach is to pick small goals we aim to prove with flight data and we construct an airframe for that one task." The X-plane philosophy is to "minimise goals, the more goals you have the more expensive it gets." For the X-59 it's about suppressing sonic booms on a budget and nothing else.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: So the stumpy little aircraft was shaped like a bullet with wings added.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: It is not exactly typical for a British party conference, let alone that of one of the smaller parties, to elicit international condemnation.
sentences.article_title: Tensions exposed among Greens by 'Zionism is racism' conference vote

sentences.text: Yet that is the position the Green Party of England and Wales is in today after Israel's foreign ministry said it was banning their leader, Zack Polanski, from entering the country.
sentences.article_title: Tensions exposed among Greens by 'Zionism is racism' conference vote

sentences.text: The cause was the motion proposed by party members and adopted by the conference on Sunday, declaring Zionism, which is the belief in the right to a Jewish homeland, to be racism.
sentences.article_title: Tensions exposed among Greens by 'Zionism is racism' conference vote

sentences.text: The Green motion describes Zionism as an ideology supporting "an ethnonationalist Jewish state", and supports instead a "single democratic Palestinian state in all of historic Palestine".
sentences.article_title: Tensions exposed among Greens by 'Zionism is racism' conference vote

sentences.text: It's hardly likely that Polanski or indeed many Greens are going to be much troubled by Israel's condemnation of the motion.
sentences.article_title: Tensions exposed among Greens by 'Zionism is racism' conference vote

sentences.text: One major factor in the Greens' electoral gains over the past year or so, a hugely successful period for the party, has been their clear and vocal condemnation of Israel's war in Gaza and actions in the region more generally.
sentences.article_title: Tensions exposed among Greens by 'Zionism is racism' conference vote

sentences.text: What may be more troubling for the Greens institutionally is what this episode reveals about some of the dynamics in the party.
sentences.article_title: Tensions exposed among Greens by 'Zionism is racism' conference vote

sentences.text: Many Greens are proud of the party's internal democracy: this motion was proposed by and voted on by party members.
sentences.article_title: Tensions exposed among Greens by 'Zionism is racism' conference vote

sentences.text: Yet that has resulted in the scenario of leading Green elected politicians facing scrutiny over party policy which the vast majority of them opposed.
sentences.article_title: Tensions exposed among Greens by 'Zionism is racism' conference vote

sentences.text: Polanski, who is not an MP, wanted changes to the motion which were rejected by the conference, and ultimately did not participate in the debate or vote.
sentences.article_title: Tensions exposed among Greens by 'Zionism is racism' conference vote

sentences.text: Of the Greens' five MPs, four opposed the motion.
sentences.article_title: Tensions exposed among Greens by 'Zionism is racism' conference vote

sentences.text: The most vocal of them was Adrian Ramsay, the MP for Waveney Valley, who was a Green co-leader for four years until September last year when he and his running mate were defeated by Polanski by a vast margin.
sentences.article_title: Tensions exposed among Greens by 'Zionism is racism' conference vote

sentences.text: Yet this may not be the last issue where that results in a public dispute between the membership and their MPs, four of whom were elected at the last general election under different leadership.
sentences.article_title: Tensions exposed among Greens by 'Zionism is racism' conference vote

sentences.text: And it is striking that, though Polanski's election as leader was a clear symbol of that shift in the Greens' approach, he did not back this motion.
sentences.article_title: Tensions exposed among Greens by 'Zionism is racism' conference vote

sentences.text: So this could presage tensions too between Polanski and the party membership, some of whom will have been inspired to join the Greens by his leadership.
sentences.article_title: Tensions exposed among Greens by 'Zionism is racism' conference vote

sentences.text: In practical terms, the Green MPs will be able to continue espousing a different position in parliament to the party's new policy.
sentences.article_title: Tensions exposed among Greens by 'Zionism is racism' conference vote

sentences.text: The Greens do not have a whipping system, meaning that MPs are free to vote as they wish.
sentences.article_title: Tensions exposed among Greens by 'Zionism is racism' conference vote

sentences.text: This is also true of their councillors, including in the almost 40 councils where the Greens are in power after the May local elections.
sentences.article_title: Tensions exposed among Greens by 'Zionism is racism' conference vote

sentences.text: It will be interesting to see whether as a result of these tensions there is a push either to constrain the ability of the party conference to make policy, or in the other direction - to constrain the ability of elected representatives to defy party policy.
sentences.article_title: Tensions exposed among Greens by 'Zionism is racism' conference vote

sentences.text: Separately, this motion may present a political headache down the line for Andy Burnham.
sentences.article_title: Tensions exposed among Greens by 'Zionism is racism' conference vote

sentences.article_title: Tensions exposed among Greens by 'Zionism is racism' conference vote

sentences.text: While Burnham did not specify what system he wanted, he said that Labour would at the next general election commit to a new system where "everyone's vote counts and everyone's voice is heard".
sentences.article_title: Tensions exposed among Greens by 'Zionism is racism' conference vote

sentences.text: Under a move to any more proportional system, on current trends, there would likely be more Green MPs as a result.
sentences.article_title: Tensions exposed among Greens by 'Zionism is racism' conference vote

sentences.article_title: Tensions exposed among Greens by 'Zionism is racism' conference vote

sentences.text: And yet the Greens are also now a party whose actions this weekend have been condemned by the Labour chair, Bridget Phillipson, as "shameful" and "fundamentally wrong".
sentences.article_title: Tensions exposed among Greens by 'Zionism is racism' conference vote

sentences.text: Angela Rayner, the communities secretary, said the Zionism motion "crosses a line and is rightly being condemned across the political spectrum." Labour has long been divided on the question of electoral reform.
sentences.article_title: Tensions exposed among Greens by 'Zionism is racism' conference vote

sentences.text: Their leader now has a clear position in favour but the Green motion this weekend could have the unintended effect of bolstering opposition within Labour to that element of the prime minister's agenda.

sentences.article_title: Early Lampard findings could come within weeks

sentences.text: Hugo Flint Cahan, 34, was fatally attacked by Rolando Torres-Pena, 22, at a mental health trust in east London A mental health trust in east London, where a man was killed by a fellow patient , has been warned further deaths may occur unless staff issues are addressed.
sentences.article_title: Coroner warns of risk of future deaths at mental health unit where patient was killed

sentences.text: Hugo Flint Cahan, 34, was strangled by 22-year-old Rolando Torres-Pena at Newham Mental Health Centre, which provides care for acutely mentally ill men, in January 2023.
sentences.article_title: Coroner warns of risk of future deaths at mental health unit where patient was killed

sentences.text: The coroner has sent a report to the Trust and NHS England raising serious concerns about the care the two men received.
sentences.article_title: Coroner warns of risk of future deaths at mental health unit where patient was killed

sentences.text: It follows a six-day inquest in September during which the senior coroner for east London, Graeme Irvine, concluded that neglect had more than trivially contributed to Flint Cahan's death.
sentences.article_title: Coroner warns of risk of future deaths at mental health unit where patient was killed

sentences.text: On the night of Flint Cahan's death, staff on the ward were found to have been asleep on the job and on their phones for long periods.
sentences.article_title: Coroner warns of risk of future deaths at mental health unit where patient was killed

sentences.text: East London NHS Foundation Trust (ELFT) says the failings identified were "wholly unacceptable" and that it has undertaken a "significant programme of work" to improve inpatient services.
sentences.article_title: Coroner warns of risk of future deaths at mental health unit where patient was killed

sentences.text: The coroner's Prevention of Future Deaths report highlights 14 concerns.
sentences.article_title: Coroner warns of risk of future deaths at mental health unit where patient was killed

sentences.text: These include failing to carry out "timely and thorough observations" of patients, then falsifying records "in the safe knowledge that staff on duty would not report or escalate the deception".
sentences.article_title: Coroner warns of risk of future deaths at mental health unit where patient was killed

sentences.text: The document also says there were delays in starting CPR on Flint Cahan when he was discovered, that staff misled the police as to what the patients had been doing on the night of the incident, and that staff colluded with each other to take two-hour unauthorised breaks.
sentences.article_title: Coroner warns of risk of future deaths at mental health unit where patient was killed

sentences.text: Torres-Pena was given a hospital order with no time limit after pleading guilty to manslaughter by diminished responsibility in 2023.
sentences.article_title: Coroner warns of risk of future deaths at mental health unit where patient was killed

sentences.text: The coroner also raised concerns that many of the failings had been brought up at a previous inquest he'd conducted.
sentences.article_title: Coroner warns of risk of future deaths at mental health unit where patient was killed

sentences.text: "The findings in this inquest are strikingly similar to the findings of an inquest before this court in 2021, remedial measures reported in that case do not appear to have been implemented effectively by the trust", the report says.
sentences.article_title: Coroner warns of risk of future deaths at mental health unit where patient was killed

sentences.text: "Findings of dishonesty on this scale are extraordinarily rare in a coronial investigation.
sentences.article_title: Coroner warns of risk of future deaths at mental health unit where patient was killed

sentences.text: The public are entitled to expect a clear explanation of how this was allowed to happen and what is being done to ensure it never happens again," says James Cahan, the family solicitor and Hugo's cousin.
sentences.article_title: Coroner warns of risk of future deaths at mental health unit where patient was killed

sentences.text: The coroner also criticised NHS England for not making independently produced reports into patient safety at Trusts publically available.
sentences.article_title: Coroner warns of risk of future deaths at mental health unit where patient was killed

sentences.text: The inquest heard that a report commissioned after Flint Cahan's death identified some of the serious failings investigated by the coroner.
sentences.article_title: Coroner warns of risk of future deaths at mental health unit where patient was killed

sentences.text: An NHS spokesperson said "patient safety incident investigations should always be published, with any necessary redactions to protect patients' identities, while making sure the lessons and learning are clear".
sentences.article_title: Coroner warns of risk of future deaths at mental health unit where patient was killed

sentences.text: In a statement, Dr David Bridle, Chief Medical Officer for ELFT, apologised to Flint Cahan's family for the failings in his care.
sentences.article_title: Coroner warns of risk of future deaths at mental health unit where patient was killed

sentences.text: He says one member of staff on duty on the night of the incident has been sacked while four others are now under investigation by the Trust.
sentences.article_title: Coroner warns of risk of future deaths at mental health unit where patient was killed

sentences.text: "We will ensure the learning from the coroner's findings informs our continuing work to strengthen patient safety and care," says Dr Bridle.
sentences.article_title: Coroner warns of risk of future deaths at mental health unit where patient was killed

sentences.text: Andy Burnham has set out his plan to transform Britain, including by ending the existing state pension triple lock from 2030 to help fund a new national care service.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: In his first Labour Party conference speech as prime minister, Burnham also said he wants to pave the way for greater public control over housing, water and energy services, and potentially reform the UK's electoral system.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: After days of questions over how to fund his social care reforms in England, Burnham pointed to changing the triple lock to generate "significant savings".
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: His plans would see the state pension increase every year at least by inflation or 2.5% - but remove the automatic annual link with average earnings.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power In front of a packed hall and watched on by family and friends, Burnham spoke for more than an hour - at times pausing and appearing to hold back tears as he referred to his father, Roy, who died earlier this month .
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: Arriving on stage to the sound of "All Together Now" by Liverpool band The Farm, Burnham made the song title a theme of his speech.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: He said he wanted to "draw a line on a decade of division" and to "stop doomscrolling on posts running Britain down".
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: Burnham also told conference that he wants to "put the country on a new path" and recalled his family's "working-class aspiration" and how the government wanted to "unlock" this for others.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: There was an expectation that Burnham's time in Liverpool for his party's conference would see him flesh out his vision for the future of the country.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: In the conference hall, he offered more details albeit with some of the proposals relating to the content of the Labour manifesto at the next general election rather than delivering immediate action.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: Burnham's plan to offer free at the point of use social care in England is among those being developed so it can be put before voters in 2029.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: He said it would be "fully funded and not through borrowing".
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: Explaining his long-held ambition to make changes, he raised his family's experiences - including how his grandmother Kitty's engagement ring was "ripped from her finger and stolen in a care home".
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: He argued a national care service was a "landmark" policy that would be "as significant as the creation of the NHS itself and utterly essential to securing its future".
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: Before turning to the pension triple lock changes, Burnham accepted he may "pay a political price" by trying to make the reforms but argued "someone has to go through the pain barrier and rip the plaster off".
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: The triple lock was introduced in 2010 by the coalition government and designed to ensure the value of the state pension was not overtaken by the increase in the cost of living or the incomes of working people.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: It means the state pension rates rise every April by either inflation, earnings growth or 2.5% - whichever is the highest.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: Burnham said this will stay in place until 2030, at which point he would like to "adjust it".
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: He said: "The state pension will continue to rise every year at least by prices or 2.5%.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: And it will hold its value relative to earnings over time so that pensioners will always share in the rising prosperity of the nation.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: "But this change will generate significant savings which we will use to build up our national care service.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: "Some may not realise it but older people with nothing more than the state pension, or only a little more, can find themselves paying care charges today from that small income.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: Under my plan, this will no longer happen." Officials have suggested the change could save £15bn a year by 2040.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: Jonathan Cribb, deputy director at the Institute for Fiscal Studies, said savings "are likely to be relatively small in the first few years, but rise substantially over time".
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: He also said "we should not expect this reform to save enough that it could fund universal social care in the next parliament".
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: The political backlash was immediate.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: Mark and Roberta Harrison say Hobie was funny and mischievous The police watchdog has criticised a force after call handlers told a family raising mental health concerns to ring a locksmith.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: On 6 August 2025, Hobie Harrison's parents called Norfolk Police to request a welfare check after he failed to respond to them.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: He was found dead the next day.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: The Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) said the force's 101 call handlers should have referred the family to mental health services, but instead suggested they contacted a locksmith.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: Norfolk Police said it was reviewing the findings and it had been following the force's Right Care, Right Person (RCRP) policy , external , which limits officer attendance at welfare calls to cases involving "immediate risk to life".
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: The IOPC said the call handlers should have asked more probing questions to assess Hobie's level of risk and there should have been a better explanation to his parents about why officers were not sent under its RCRP guidelines.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: Hobie's parents, Mark and Roberta Harrison, made a second request for a welfare check for their son to Norfolk Police the following day.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: Officers attended and found the 30-year-old dead in his flat in Norwich.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: The couple say they were left unsure where to turn after being told their concerns for their son did not meet the threshold for a police response In October 2025, the family made a complaint to Norfolk Police over its handling of their call.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: In its report, the IOPC criticised Norfolk Police's response to that complaint after the force told the parents officers should not have attended either call, including the second one that led to Hobie's body being found.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: The IOPC called that reply "unnecessary and insensitive".
