sentences.text: Hobie had previously threatened suicide and Mark said: "We'll never know whether he was still alive when we first called and whether something could have been done.

sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: Overcoming social anxiety can be tricky but experts have shared some tips to try and make it easier It was during her teenage years that Mary began to become anxious in social situations.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: It got so bad she developed depression and had to have time off school.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: By the time she started university, she avoided group settings altogether.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "I didn't join clubs and societies like others did," says Mary (not her real name).
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "I just thought nobody would want to get to know me.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: I didn't really make a single friend during my whole degree." Mary's social anxiety was so bad that she was diagnosed as having social anxiety disorder - something that affects up to 12% of people , external at some point in their lives.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: But plenty more report struggling more generally.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: As students return to uni, we asked experts how to overcome these feelings whether in your first, or final year.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: This video can not be played What makes you socially anxious?
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: Research has suggested more than a fifth of university students face some kind of social anxiety during their studies – and it has been linked to lower grades, poorer relationships and isolation in a study by the universities of Chichester, Coventry and University College London , external .
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: For many, university marks the first time they have moved out of home – and the expectation is that they will quickly make friends.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: Mary, who went to the University of Exeter, says she did try.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "When I first got there I went to one society, but everybody was talking to each other and I had a sudden fear come over me.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: I felt I wouldn't fit in and I went home." Mary, who is now 25, describes her social anxiety as like an out of body experience.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: When she was talking to new people, heat would rise in her face and her hands would begin to tingle.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "I'd almost feel myself separating from my body.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: I forgot how to form words," she says.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "After social situations I was often left with the sense that I'd done something awful.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: I had an all-consuming feel of shame.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: I kept thinking there was something fundamentally flawed in me." Neil Greening, chair of the Social Anxiety Alliance UK, says this is a typical characteristic of people with social anxiety.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "People think they have a personality flaw.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: They internalise it rather than seeing it as a recognisable condition that they can get help for." The key thing to remember: It's fairly normal to feel a little shy or anxious when meeting new people, being in new situations or going for a job interview.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: Social anxiety is when it actually stops people doing things, Greening says.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: For those with a clinical diagnosis it can have a debilitating impact like it did for Mary.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "It can be hard to admit to any form of social anxiety in a world where extrovertism and social confidence is generally admired.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: Mary, who has moved on to do a postgraduate course, is now managing her social anxiety better.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: After her undergraduate degree she got support from the NHS in the form of a talking therapy called CBT.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: It is considered the gold standard treatment for social anxiety and encourages people to re-frame their thoughts and change their behaviours.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: Prof David Clark, a psychologist at the University of Oxford, says he would like to see more people come forward for therapy but says people can also take steps to help themselves.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: The first step, he says, is to stop obsessive self-focus .
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "People with social anxiety often monitor themselves constantly during social situations.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "Focus outwardly on the conversation, other person or your surroundings." He says you also need to test your fears with behavioural experiments by asking a question in a meeting or saying something in a group and noticing what happens.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "People with social anxiety often assume negative outcomes – that they will embarrass themselves or think others will find them boring.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: Testing that can help people break that.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: It's frightening, but it can really help." He also says they need to drop safety behaviours , such as rehearsing every sentence, avoiding eye contact or sticking close to one particular person.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: And finally, Clark adds, try to avoid post-event rumination .
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "It's so easy to distort what actually happened." This is something Mary can empathise with.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "I used to play things over constantly in my mind.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: What I've learnt is that dealing with social anxiety is a gradual process.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: The therapy really helped me, but so did something a friend said to me a couple of years ago.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "When I said I didn't want to join her in meeting some of her friends, citing my poor social skills, she said she'd never thought that about me and that I shouldn't undersell myself.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: I was overcome with emotion.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "I'm now pushing myself to engage more.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: It helps that in my postgrad course we're in smaller groups, but I've also joined an astronomy group.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: It's still difficult and it doesn't always go how I want it to, but I'm learning to manage it." Fresh bedsheets and dusk walks: Expert tips for sleep-deprived freshers Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse Why caffeine makes some people buzz - and others barely notice

sentences.text: A new NHS-style social care system for England could take decades to be implemented, economist Sir Andrew Dilnot has told the BBC.

sentences.text: Have you ever slept next to a snoring partner and woken up feeling stressed, unfocused or forgetful the next day?
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: As snoring is relatively common, it is often left untreated and dismissed as a harmless irritation.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: But according to experts, sleeping next to a snorer could be impacting your health.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Snoring is caused by the vibration of the soft tissues in our upper airways during sleep, explains Dr Clare Simon, a dentist with a special interest in dental sleep medicine.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: About 40% of the UK adult population snores, with the issue affecting more men than women, says the British Snoring and Sleep Apnoea Association (BSSAA).
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: And 75% of people with a snoring partner say they have had their sleep impacted, according to a US survey by the Sleep Foundation.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Here's what you need to know about the impact on partners - and what you can do about it.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Prof Ama Johal, a consultant orthodontist and sleep expert at Aerox Health, explains that the partner of a snorer can become "so impacted upon that it's almost a last-ditch effort on their part to get up and go sleep in a separate room because they have to sleep".
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: He adds: "As humans we physically can't function without that necessity." Prof Ama Johal says many couples put up with the negative effects snoring for too long During the night, we cycle through different stages of sleep in repeating patterns, usually every 90 minutes.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: The deeper stages of this cycle are important for physical restoration.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: If sleep is frequently disrupted, you may spend less time in the restorative stages, meaning you can wake up feeling tired, even if you've spent a lot of time in bed, the BSSAA explains.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Your brain processes and stores information from the day during sleep.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Fragmented sleep - which can happen if you're waking up due to a snoring partner - can interrupt this process, impacting your focus and memory.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Disrupted sleep can also impact hormone regulation, which affects your energy levels and motivation.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Sleep also plays a role in regulating the brain systems involved in stress and emotional response.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: When it is disrupted, these systems can become less balanced, which may make you feel more irritable and less able to cope with stress.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: This is something Meg Warren, 29, experienced when her former partner's snoring would keep her up.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: She says: "Without fail, after a snoring-induced wake up I would feel on incredibly high alert." Meg, a charity media officer, would prod him throughout the night and try to coax him from his back to his side.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: She says she would wake up "feeling groggy and dazed, sometimes so much so that it would feel like a hangover".

sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: These devices vary, but in general they all provide users with a report of their night, broken down by sleep stages - time awake, light sleep, deep sleep, and REM (rapid eye movement).

sentences.text: Many also give users a "sleep score".
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

One proposed lawsuit against Oura, filed last month in San Francisco, alleges that Oura rings are unable to accurately measure sleep quality and sleep stages, and instead rely on AI-generated estimates that have "a coin flip's chance of being correct".

sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: This is something Jess Hill says she noticed in herself after getting a Garmin watch several years ago.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Sarah Mackay, known as @fitwsarah online, says her energy levels change through her cycle A woman points to a colour-coded grid dividing the menstrual cycle into four phases, each paired with a different list of exercises.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "When you're bleeding, you want to be doing steady-pace jogging, Pilates, barre, walking, resting," she tells viewers.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: This is one of thousands of videos on TikTok and Instagram suggesting that people change their workouts depending on where they are in their menstrual cycles - something known as 'cycle-syncing'.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: So-called cycle-syncing workout plans have surged in popularity online, with Google searches for the term rising 740% since 2022 and more than 55,000 TikTok videos now using the #cyclesyncing hashtag.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Most of the advice is shared by fitness and wellness creators rather than medical or research experts.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Kelly McNulty, a researcher at Leeds Beckett University specialising in menstrual cycles and exercise, says there is evidence that some women experience changes in symptoms, energy or perceived strength across their cycle.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: But that is different from evidence that all women should train in a particular way at a particular point, she tells the BBC, adding that these videos are "a trend based on marketing rather than any kind of research or evidence".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "There isn't any research to support that kind of phase-based prescription," she says.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: This video can not be played Should you sync your exercise routine with your period?
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: A key issue is that menstrual cycles are highly individual, McNulty adds - they can differ between women, and one woman's experience can also change from one cycle to the next.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: That makes the blanket advice often found on social media difficult to apply, she explains.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Many cycle-tracking apps and programmes are also designed around relatively regular menstrual cycles that are 21 to 35 days, which can make their recommendations less applicable to people with irregular periods, or those using hormonal contraception.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: She doesn't follow a prescriptive plan, she says, but instead makes changes intuitively.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "In my luteal phase I'll try and ease off in the training," she tells the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "In my follicular phase, I'm so energised, I feel like I can lift so much heavier.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: I like to try and get my long runs in." Burgoyne also welcomes the growing attention on women's health, and says that exercise and nutrition research has historically focused heavily on male bodies, with findings then often applied to women.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Sarah says she has sometimes hit personal records while on her period Fitness creator Sarah Mackay, known as @liftwsarah on Instagram and TikTok, has also noticed her energy, motivation, cramps and mood change through the month.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: But she deliberately avoids strict plans because, she says, "there are too many variables at play".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Some online plans advise women to avoid intense training during their period, she says, yet she has sometimes hit personal records while menstruating.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "The problem is not that the menstrual cycle is irrelevant," she says, but that "not everything is predictable".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Dr Faye Bate, a trained medical doctor and women's health expert, is also wary of advice suggesting all women should train differently according to their menstrual phase.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "A one-size-fits-all model of 'you should be exercising this way in this phase and a different way in a different phase' shouldn't be advice that applies to all women," she says.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: She is concerned that repeatedly telling women they are likely to be weaker or less capable at particular points in their cycle could create a "nocebo" effect - where negative expectations themselves influence how someone feels or performs.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: McNulty tells the BBC that routinely easing off resistance training could also limit progress.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Strength training is particularly important for women, who face a higher risk of osteoporosis later in life.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: While cycle-syncing itself may not be backed by strong evidence, the experts we spoke to did suggest being "cycle-aware".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: McNulty says tracking your cycle can be a useful way to understand your own patterns, while Dr Bate also encourages women to become more familiar with how they feel at different points in the month.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Both welcome the fact that menstrual health is being discussed more openly, but say the focus should be on individual experience, rather than rigid, phase-based rules.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: In practice, that might mean having painkillers ready before your period, taking a rest day when symptoms are worse, or easing off a workout if you feel unusually fatigued.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: For Dr Bate, "the most important part is tuning in to how you feel".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: In other words, use your cycle as information rather than a set of rules.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: As temperatures exceed 30C (86F) in some parts of the UK this week, the last thing people want to do is turn on the oven.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Not only can cooking in hot weather feel like a chore, but many of us find ourselves feeling less hungry altogether.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So when the heat gets too much, should we consider changing our diet?
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Here are three things to think about next time you're hot and hungry.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking chicken in an air fryer uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven "There's no need for more protein in a heatwave," says Aisling Daly, senior lecturer in nutrition at Oxford Brookes University.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But if you fancy it, some of the most common proteins will need cooking (like meat, chicken and fish) and that can be off-putting in the heat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even an outdoor BBQ can be too hot to handle.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking a chicken leg in the worktop device uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven, according to Radio 4's Sliced Bread .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And because they are smaller and speedier, they also pump less heat into your kitchen.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But experts say don't forget about your slightly less fashionable slow cooker - likely buried in the back of your cupboard.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even though they run for longer, they're typically more energy efficient and release even less heat than the air fryer.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: The reality, though, is that simply by eating and digesting protein, our bodies produce more heat than other food groups.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: That's due to the energy needed by the stomach, intestines and liver to break down and absorb these complex molecules.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So that steak you crave will only bring you out in a sweat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But you can also get your protein from lentils, nuts, milk, tofu and cheese too.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: To reduce body heat while still getting your protein fix, Dr Daly recommends focusing on things like bean salads, eggs, pre-cooked meats and plenty of Greek yoghurt (frozen too).
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Making a smoothie by blending up fruit, veg and yogurt (while adding in peanut butter for protein) can provide a balanced, nutritious meal in an easy way.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And it might also be time to turn to some lighter fish, such as tuna, salmon or prawns.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: When it's hot, we lose water when we sweat, so we need to replace it or we become dehydrated.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Six to eight glasses of fluid a day is normally recommended by the NHS, , external and in a heatwave you could need a lot more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "There is no single amount that suits everyone, because how much fluid your body needs depends on lots of factors like your age, body size, activity levels and health status," says Dr Charlotte Mills, food and nutrition scientist at the University of Reading.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: World Cup footballers aren't the only ones who benefit from hydration breaks: other athletes and pregnant and breastfeeding women are among those who need to drink more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But rehydrating doesn't just mean refilling your water bottle every couple of hours.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "We need to eat our water as well as drink it," says Dr Daly, "80-90% of fruit and vegetables are full of water." Cucumber, tomatoes, lettuce, celery, watermelon and strawberries all have very high water content, above 90%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Apples, carrots, cooked broccoli and pears contain 80% to 89% water, as do oranges, grapes and pineapple.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: In comparison, boiled eggs are 75% water , external , with digestive biscuits only 2.8% water , external .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even a cheese and tomato pizza is 38% water, with takeaway chips containing as much as 51%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: If your mouth has dried up just reading this, try some of these water-rich recipes .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: A useful way to check if you're hydrated is to check the colour of your urine.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Pale yellow is what you're after.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: If it's orangey or dark brown, that's a sign that your kidneys - which filter waste products and produce urine - are holding onto water because there isn't enough in the body.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: That means you're dehydrated and need to drink more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Warm or room-temperature drinks are just as good as cold ones for cooling you down We know some people love a cuppa, even when it's sweltering, and that actually makes scientific sense.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Warm or room-temperature drinks are just as good as cold ones for cooling you down, says Dr Daly.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Research suggests your body sweats more quickly to get rid of the excess heat after a hot drink.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: After a cold drink, your body sweats more slowly.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Your body is trying to keep your core temperature steady at about 37 degrees celsius.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So hot tea won't necessarily help you cool down more quickly - the key thing is to stay hydrated no matter the temperature of the liquid.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: You don't need to shun your favourite coffee either just because it's hot - although too much caffeine can make the body produce more urine, and leave you dehydrated.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: For matcha fans, the drink contains more caffeine than a cup of tea but less than a regular coffee.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Dr Daly says one or two coffees a day should make little difference to your hydration levels - but five or six will start to have an effect.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Bear in mind that drinking alcohol also dehydrates.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: You could structure your day differently too, and take a southern European approach to eating.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Have an early breakfast, an afternoon siesta while it's very hot and then a late dinner.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Periods of hot weather can affect anyone, but some people run a greater risk of serious harm.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Experts recommend that those who may be more vulnerable - such as older people and babies and young children - should take extra precautions.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: As the body gets hotter, blood vessels open up.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: This lowers your blood pressure and makes your heart work harder to push the blood around the body.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: This process can cause mild symptoms such as an itchy heat rash or swollen feet.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: At the same time, sweating leads to the loss of fluids and salt and, crucially, the balance between them in the body changes.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: This, combined with the lowered blood pressure, can lead to heat exhaustion.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Symptoms include: If blood pressure drops too far, the risk of heart attacks rises.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: How does sunscreen work, and how much do you need to use?
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Staying safe in water when the weather's hot Our bodies strive to keep a core temperature of about 37C whether we are in a snowstorm or a heatwave.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: That is the temperature at which our bodies have evolved to work.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: But as the weather gets hotter, it is harder for the body to keep its core temperature down.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: It opens more blood vessels near the skin to lose heat to our surroundings and starts sweating.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: As the sweat evaporates, it dramatically increases the heat lost from the skin.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: No one - especially babies, young children and animals - should ever be left in a locked vehicle.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Hot weather: How to sleep in the heat Six ways to keep your home and yourself cool in hot weather When is it too hot to walk your dog?
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: If you see someone you think has heat exhaustion , the NHS says you should: , external move them to a cool place get them to lie down and raise their feet slightly get them to drink plenty of water - sports or rehydration drinks are also OK cool their skin - spray or sponge them with cool water and fan them.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Cold packs around the armpits or neck are also good If they can be cooled down within half an hour, then heat exhaustion is not normally serious.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: However, if they do not recover within 30 minutes, then they are at risk of heatstroke .
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: This is a medical emergency and you should call 999 immediately.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: People with heatstroke may stop sweating even though they are too hot.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Their temperature could go over 40C and they might have seizures or lose consciousness.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: What to do if you think someone has heat exhaustion or heatstroke People who are older or have some long-term conditions - such as heart disease -  are sometimes less able to cope with the strain heat puts on the body.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Diabetes can make the body lose water more quickly and some complications of the disease can alter blood vessels and the ability to sweat.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Children and those who are less mobile may also be more vulnerable.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Brain diseases, such as dementia, can also leave people unaware of the heat or unable to do anything about it.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: People who are homeless will also be more exposed to the sun.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Those living in top-floor flats will also face higher temperatures.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Yes - but the NHS says people should keep taking their medication as normal, and focus on staying cool and hydrated.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Diuretics - sometimes called "water pills" - increase the amount of water the body expels.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: They are taken widely, including for heart failure.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: In high temperatures, they increase the dangers of dehydration and imbalances in key minerals in the body.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Antihypertensives - which lower blood pressure - can combine with the blood vessels that are dilating to cope with the heat and cause dangerous drops in blood pressure.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Some drugs for people with epilepsy and Parkinson's can block sweating and make it harder for the body to cool itself.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Other drugs such as lithium or statins can become more concentrated and problematic in the blood if there is too much fluid loss.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: During 2022 - which saw the highest recorded temperature in England at 40.3C - there were an estimated 2,985 so-called "excess deaths" as a result of the heat , external , the most recorded in any given year.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: There were an estimated 1,311 heat-associated deaths , external during summer 2024, and an estimated 1,504 , external during summer 2025.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Most heat-related excess deaths are due to heart attacks and strokes caused by the strain of trying to keep body temperatures stable.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: The higher death rate starts to kick in once the thermometer passes 25C-26C.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: However, evidence suggests the deaths tend to be caused by higher temperatures in spring or early summer rather than during "peak summer".
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: This could be because we start to change our day-to-day behaviour as summer progresses and we get more used to dealing with the heat.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: The evidence from previous heatwaves is the increase in deaths happens very quickly - within the first 24 hours of a heatwave.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Dr Amara Naseem says GPs are under pressure to offer more appointments, rather than a focus on quality treatment Pressure to provide more GP appointments is making it harder to include checks for gynaecological cancers within the 10-minute slots, doctors have said.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: Dr Amara Naseem says her clinics always overrun as it takes about 20 minutes to sensitively take a detailed history and carry out internal examinations.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: A reduced number of practices in her area means she has taken on more patients and fears there is a risk that women will not raise gynaecological symptoms or attend screenings if appointments are rushed, painful or not handled well.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: The Welsh government said it was increasing investment in primary care and recruiting up to 100 extra GPs.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: Research by cancer charity Tenovus, in support of Claire's Campaign , external , found about half of the 100 GPs surveyed across Wales felt limited consultation time was a major concern.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: A third also had concerns about "over-referring" people for further testing to rule out cancers, given hospitals are already overstretched.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: Currently, 95% of patients put on the suspected cancer pathway are later told they do not have cancer.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: But doctors said teasing out the cancer cases at an early stage could be challenging when symptoms such as bloating are hard to distinguish from benign conditions including irritable bowel syndrome.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: Naseem said the pressure from the Welsh government was to "offer more appointments to the patient, rather than about the quality of the treatment".
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: Lowri Griffiths of Tenovus said incidence and mortality rates for gynaecological cancers in Wales were higher than the UK average - something she added the Welsh government needed "to get to grips with".
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: Pledges to increase GP numbers were promising, she said, "but unless we address both the primary care setting and the hospital setting, the system won't work".
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: Lowri Griffiths says Wales needs to be "more aspirational" in gynaecological care Naseem said many women's health issues may require an internal examination, which requires time to be done "in an empathetic and sensitive way".
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: She added: "I'm working in a very diverse community, also in a deprived community, where uptake of screening is already low." She said in communities where myths existed around screening, time is also required to explain what is involved and allay fears and potentially work with interpreters.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: Dr Kathrin Thomas said her friend Claire O'Shea was "a real feminist" Dr Kathrin Thomas, a former GP and public health specialist, got involved in Claire's Campaign when her friend Claire O'Shea was given a late diagnosis for a gynaecological cancer.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: Claire, from Cardiff, died last year, aged 42.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: Thomas said GP numbers in Wales had "almost flat-lined" while the workload had increased, especially in more disadvantaged areas where there were "fewer doctors, fewer nurses and the healthcare needs are much greater".
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: She is also involved with Deep End Cymru - a network of GP practices in the most deprived areas.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: "We've got a big difference in the cancer experience in more deprived communities - cervical cancer in particular," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: "There's a wide inequity between women in more affluent areas and women in poorer areas." Of the 1,200 women diagnosed, about 470 patients die from a gynaecological cancer, either of the womb (uterine), ovary, cervix, vulva or vagina, in Wales each year.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: Screening is only available for cervical cancer and it does not detect other cancers.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: "Cancer outcomes are improving dramatically over the decades, but we're struggling in Wales to get the outcomes that other richer countries are getting," said Thomas.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: The waiting times for gynaecological cancer treatment in Wales have improved significantly over the past year, from 34% of patients being treated within 62 days, to 51.3%.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: However, the most recent Wales average for all cancers was 60.1% against a target of 75%.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: Maria Bailey has been fundraising to make more "grab and go" bags for other patients treated for cervical cancer.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: Thomas said continuity of care came up repeatedly among the Tenovus survey of GPs.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: "You have a 20% less chance of dying if you have the same team that looks after you," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: Maria Bailey feels being able to see the same GP was a factor in her own cervical cancer diagnosis.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: "I feel really lucky that she took me seriously from the off.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: She knows me - she knew I was alarmed and [the symptoms] weren't normal for me.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: She took it very seriously," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: The 55-year-old from Pencoed, Bridgend county, experienced increased fatigue and light vaginal bleeding but put it down to working extra hours and the menopause.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: But in February she spoke to her GP after the bleeding intensified.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: "It was heavy bleeding and quite large clots, which I've never had before - they looked like baby seals and that was really alarming." An internal examination followed by a raft of further tests uncovered a 4cm (1.5in) tumour and grade 2 cancer , external around her cervix.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: "I was in shock, but as soon as they said it wasn't life-threatening, that was it.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: It was just one gear - and that was go." Maria underwent chemotherapy, radiotherapy and brachytherapy , external across centres in Swansea and Cardiff and has since been raising money to provide essential provisions for others going through treatment for cervical cancer.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: "I'm quite an organised person and don't like walking into anything blind," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: But an online search for advice about the things needed when starting treatment yielded very little.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: She has now donated several "Bailey's bags" to two cancer centres containing items such as a water bottle, strong-flavoured sweets to overcome the metallic taste treatment can leave, a foldable fan, neck cushion, battery pack for USB devices and a medication box.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: The Welsh government said: "We're committed to strengthening primary care as the foundation of the NHS in Wales.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: "We've urged health boards to shift more resources towards primary and community care, with a further primary care summit planned to track their progress.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: Sally Williams told the BBC how isolated she became during the "run-up" to menopause For three years, Sally Williams struggled to understand what was happening to her as her mental health deteriorated and her life fell apart, spending almost 11 months in hospital across eight admissions.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: She left her finance job, was separated from her teenage son and found herself fighting for her life, unaware her symptoms could be linked to perimenopause.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: "No one joined the dots," Williams said.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: I joined the dots and it was transformational to start hormone replacement therapy and literally come back to life." Williams, who initially self-diagnosed, wants other women to be aware of perimenopause, the years leading up to menopause, which she described as the "danger zone".
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: Perimenopause , external , which commonly begins around the age of 46, is when women experience menopause symptoms while still having periods.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: Symptoms can include anxiety, mood swings, brain fog, hot flushes and irregular periods, with some women taking hormone replacement therapy (HRT) to help  alleviate the symptoms.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: What is the menopause and what are the main signs?
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: How does Hormone replacement therapy (HRT) work?
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: When her symptoms began in her late 40s, Williams, from the Wychavon area, said doctors she saw initially thought she had depression.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: "I had multiple attempts on my life, two significant ones, one where I was in a wheelchair for three months for polytrauma, and this was in Covid, so there were no visitors.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: I had no contact with anyone," she explained.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: This was at perimenopause time.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: My message to women is that, menopause is not the danger zone, it's the run up, it's the 45 to 54." For Williams, who said she was "unrecognisable" before her eventual diagnosis, it was HRT which eventually helped her, but she said it may not be for everyone.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: The drug , which isn't suitable for some women, tops up and stabilises oestrogen levels, sometimes in combination with a synthetic or bioidentical version of progesterone.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: Williams is set to speak about her hard fought menopause diagnosis at Meno Fest at Worcester Rugby Club on 7 October , external , as part of Menopause Awareness Month.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: The free event is being held with the aim of helping people to gain greater understanding of how perimenopause and menopause can affect every aspect of life from physical and mental health to relationships, work and family life.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: Williams told the BBC of how isolated she became during the "run-up" to menopause.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: I didn't see my friends, my family for three years and I was a recluse.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: And my son, who was in his teens, I probably saw him three times," she explained.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: "He had leave his school and his friends and he had to go and live with his dad because he couldn't see me.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: I couldn't care for him." It was also important that men recognised what was happening to women during perimenopause, she added.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: "I think men need to come into the conversation as well, and I'm not just talking husbands and partners, I'm talking sons," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: "It was devastating and there's relationships that have been broken that will never be put back together.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: I'm very sad about that." If you have been affected by the issues in this story, help and support is available via the BBC Action Line .
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: Rosanna Brown was advised to end her pregnancy because her baby had a life-threatening medical condition A woman whose baby was too ill to be born is calling for better awareness of choosing a termination for medical reasons.
sentences.article_title: Baby termination was 'our most loving choice'

sentences.text: Rosanna Brown, who lives near Waterlooville, Hampshire, was advised to end her pregnancy with son William in 2023 because he had a rare and life-threatening medical condition called Chaos syndrome.
sentences.article_title: Baby termination was 'our most loving choice'

sentences.text: Continuing the pregnancy would have risked both their lives, but Rosanna said the experience was made even more difficult due to a lack of training around medically-advised abortions.
sentences.article_title: Baby termination was 'our most loving choice'

sentences.text: An NHS spokesperson said it offered "comprehensive support for women whose unborn baby is diagnosed with a serious health condition".
sentences.article_title: Baby termination was 'our most loving choice'

sentences.text: Rosanna said she understood why so many people who suffered a termination for medical reasons (TFMR) just told others they had had a miscarriage.
sentences.article_title: Baby termination was 'our most loving choice'

sentences.text: "Because it's a type of abortion, you have the pro-life pro-choice argument, you are thrown into the middle of that," she said.
sentences.article_title: Baby termination was 'our most loving choice'

sentences.text: "You have this feeling that your grief isn't as valid because you've chosen [it].
sentences.article_title: Baby termination was 'our most loving choice'

sentences.text: "It's such a complex and lonely thing to go through and it's so much harder if you can't tell the truth of what happened to you.
sentences.article_title: Baby termination was 'our most loving choice'

sentences.text: "Because for so many parents, termination is the most loving thing they could offer." About 5,000 women a year are offered a TFMR, which is more than experience stillbirth and neonatal death.
sentences.article_title: Baby termination was 'our most loving choice'

sentences.text: Jane Fisher from the Arc charity said it was important to break the taboo around TFMR Rosanna is campaigning for change, including for the term TFMR to be properly used, which she said it was not on her son's forms.
sentences.article_title: Baby termination was 'our most loving choice'

sentences.text: Instead her loss was described as a "late miscarriage", which she said "silences you further".
sentences.article_title: Baby termination was 'our most loving choice'

sentences.text: "I made a choice here, I didn't naturally lose my baby," she said.
sentences.article_title: Baby termination was 'our most loving choice'

sentences.text: "I didn't come across [TFMR] until a good few months after I'd lost him.
sentences.article_title: Baby termination was 'our most loving choice'

sentences.text: And in that time, you're searching for community and for support and for compassion for people to get it.
sentences.article_title: Baby termination was 'our most loving choice'

sentences.text: "And if that term is not being used by medical professionals with the patients that they're seeing, I think sometimes it's because they're worried about offending you." Jane Fisher, chief executive of the ARC Charity, said it was a very difficult situation and that using the right term was really important.
sentences.article_title: Baby termination was 'our most loving choice'

sentences.text: "It describes the reality of the situation and I think that's important both for parents to accept what happened but also for us to break the stigma and taboo around this particular loss," she said.
sentences.article_title: Baby termination was 'our most loving choice'

sentences.text: She added without that, it could be "very difficult to grieve in a healthy way".
sentences.article_title: Baby termination was 'our most loving choice'

sentences.text: Earlier this year, Rosanna and her husband became parents again to a daughter.
sentences.article_title: Baby termination was 'our most loving choice'

sentences.text: But they said they would always talk about her big brother William and had planted a memorial garden in his honour.
sentences.article_title: Baby termination was 'our most loving choice'

sentences.text: Ahead of Baby Loss Awareness Week, she has written and published a compassionate guide to help others, called The Silence Of TFMR.
sentences.article_title: Baby termination was 'our most loving choice'

sentences.text: She said: "Some of the most painful advice [was] 'don't let this define you'.
sentences.article_title: Baby termination was 'our most loving choice'

sentences.text: I really took offence because your identity changes, your whole life changes.
sentences.article_title: Baby termination was 'our most loving choice'

sentences.text: "I am defined [by it] and am quite happy to be.
sentences.article_title: Baby termination was 'our most loving choice'

sentences.text: I need to find ways to keep tapping into that identity of parent to him because that's the only way he gets to exist, in this world." Baby Loss Awareness Week takes place from 9 to 15 October.
sentences.article_title: Baby termination was 'our most loving choice'

sentences.article_title: Survey to show 'vital insight' of children's lives

sentences.text: Chief statistician Ian Cope said it provided a "vital insight" into the lives of children and young people on the island.
sentences.article_title: Survey to show 'vital insight' of children's lives

sentences.text: Dr Chris McCarthy says the pillow that's best for you depends on the way you sleep (branding has been obscured) "I am one of those people," says Dr Chris McCarthy.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: "I do take my pillow with me." You may have seen those people at the airport - a pillow stuffed under an arm as they drag their suitcases to check-in.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Or you might be one yourself - attached to a pillow that's soft enough to settle into but robust enough that it's not bunched into a ball by morning.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: McCarthy insists he's not being fussy.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: He's a top physiotherapist and knows the wrong pillow can be a pain in the neck.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: He doesn't take his abroad, but as soon as he gets to his hotel he starts "faffing about" with the pillows - and he's got a tried and tested trick to make even the most lacklustre one fit for sleep.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Here's his guide to choosing the perfect pillow for you.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: What makes the perfect pillow?
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: One advertised for your sleeping position?
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Sliced Bread separates science fact from the marketing fiction.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: McCarthy, an associate professor at the Manchester School of Physiotherapy, says the right pillow will depend on what position you sleep in.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: He tells the BBC's Sliced Bread podcast that most people fall into one of three categories of sleeper: side, back or front.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: McCarthy discourages front sleeping as your neck is turned one way for a long period of time.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: "Inevitably a muscle or ligament gets stretched and a bit irritated," he says.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: "If there's one thing there's a really good consensus on... in the physiotherapy world about treating spinal pain, it's don't sleep on your front." When choosing a pillow, back sleepers should consider the flexion at the top of their spine, a curving that increases naturally in many people as they age.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: If you have a bigger bend "it means you need a slightly thicker pillow than someone who's got a very flat back," says McCarthy.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: For side sleepers the key measurement is the width of your shoulders.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: In general, the broader you are the thicker the pillow you will need.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: But you also need to consider your mattress.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: McCarthy says how much you sink into your mattress "makes a huge difference in the subsequent height you then need from the pillow".
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: "Broad shoulders need a thick pillow [if] you're on a very firm mattress," he explains.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: "If you're on a softer mattress, then you need a thinner pillow because your shoulder sinks into the mattress [more]." This is less of an issue for back sleepers as they don't sink into the mattress as much as side sleepers do.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: If your pillow feels too flat, McCarthy suggests placing a folded towel underneath and changing the number of folds to adjust the height.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Then you can make a rough measurement to help you pick a new one.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Specialist pillows are often advertised as contoured, ergonomic or orthopaedic - but McCarthy says their effectiveness isn't completely proven.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: "There is a little bit of fairly scrappy evidence to suggest that having a little bit of a higher front of the pillow, which goes into the neck area... does help [side sleepers]." To see if a higher front helps you sleep better, you can try McCarthy's towel trick by rolling it and placing it underneath your pillow.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: He urges side sleepers to pick a position that keeps their back straight.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: For back sleepers, some manufacturers advertise a pillow with a dip in the middle that is raised at the sides.

sentences.text: Ofcom is investigating whether Meta breached its duties under the UK's online safety laws with the launch of its "Instants" feature on Instagram.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: The tool - allowing users to take and share an instant image with close friends, that disappears once viewed - was launched on Meta's photo-sharing app in May as "a new way to share photos in the moment".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: But the regulator said the social media giant had not properly assessed risks posed by the feature prior to launching it - something it is required to do under the UK's Online Safety Act (OSA).
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: A Meta spokesperson said in a statement that it "takes its regulatory obligations under the Online Safety Act seriously".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "We conducted a risk analysis and briefed Ofcom about this feature on a number of occasions before launching it," they said.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "We will of course co-operate with Ofcom during this investigation." Ofcom said its probe would examine whether Meta breached OSA duties by not carrying out "a suitable and sufficient illegal content risk assessment and children's risk assessment before the launch of Instants".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Under the UK's sweeping online safety rules, platforms including Meta must carry out and update risk assessments to comply with a range of duties, including to tackle illegal content.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: They must also show how they prevent children permitted to use their services from encountering content deemed harmful for them.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: This spans material relating to pornography, or promoting self-harm or suicide - as "priority primary content" - alongside things like abusive, hateful or bullying content.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "Our online safety laws are clear – significant changes to platforms must be risk assessed before they're launched," said Ofcom enforcement director George Lusty.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "This is a vital step that tech firms must take to protect their users," he added.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Images shared with Instants can be viewed by those who have been selected as "close friends" by a user, or those who they follow and are followed back by.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Meta says the feature has a range of built-in protections, including for younger users with Teen Accounts, including preventing screenshots, reshares or forwarding of Instants.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: But disappearing messages and images have been singled out previously as posing particular risks for child or teen users of some apps .
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "Safety by design must be built in, not bolted on, and today's investigation shows we'll take action where we have concerns that providers are failing to comply," Lusty added.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: It also contends that its messaging and image-sharing apps should not have to face additional requirements under the OSA, such as tackling paid-for fraud ads.

sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas
