sentences.text: When parenting advice becomes too much Before Rosie Whitfield became a mum, she imagined herself parenting very calm children.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "Then I had two wild boys," she says with a laugh.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Following the birth of her kids, Rosie spent hours online looking for the best advice and was drawn to one particular approach to parenting: Gentle parenting, which focuses on empathy and mutual respect with little emphasis on punishment, albeit with boundaries.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: But she constantly worried her choices, from sleep schedules to handling toddler tantrums, were "ruining their lives forever".
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Rosie believes her confidence and intuition were stripped away as she questioned every parenting decision.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Government research suggests that around two-thirds of parents with young children feel overwhelmed by the amount of parenting information available and struggle with conflicting advice, with many turning to social media for support.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Rosie Whitfield says she felt overwhelmed by the amount of parenting advice online when looking for guidance on raising her two sons.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: And it's not just the early years.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Research from the charity Action for Children found that many parents of teenagers who initially contacted the charity for help with school avoidance, ADHD or mental health, often went on to describe their own anxiety, exhaustion and uncertainty of how to parent with empathy and patience when close to burnout.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Faced with an array of parenting philosophies, or "brands" to choose from, is all of this advice helping parents or making them more anxious?
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: And is there really a best way to parent?
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Or, as we strive to become the perfect parent, are we losing our intuition?
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Parents today are confronted by parenting styles including "helicopter parenting", which is focused on closely monitoring and protecting children from harm, and "tiger parenting", which involves strict parenting and high expectations for achievement.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: There are also "snowplough parents", who try to remove obstacles from their child's path, and "dolphin parents", who aim to be firm but flexible.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Author Matilda Gosling, who wrote Evidence‑Based Parenting, says many of the parenting fads or trends complicate what should be a straightforward relationship between a parent and child.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "Throughout history, you get these swings from one extreme to the other," she says.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Gentle parenting is seen by some as the latest swing away from a strict, detached parenting style popular in the 1990s, which often relied on controlled crying, the naughty step and time out.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: It is built around understanding, empathy and respect but also emphasises the importance of boundaries.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: One of the most widely studied models of parenting comes from developmental psychologist Diana Baumrind.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Baumrind identified three parenting styles, later expanded to four: authoritative (high warmth and high control), authoritarian (low warmth and high control), permissive (high warmth and low control), and neglectful (low warmth and low control).
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "Authoritative is the gold standard," says Gosling who has looked at more than 1,000 studies.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Research has found that children raised with an authoritative approach, combining warmth with clear boundaries, tend to achieve better academic results, have higher self-esteem and stronger social skills.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: But where gentle parenting fits within that framework is disputed.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Gosling believes that it falls on the permissive side.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "It's very much child-led.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: The child ends up having so much control that there's no sense of safety coming from the outside." However, Sarah Ockwell-Smith, who is widely credited with coining and popularising the term 'gentle parenting', strongly disagrees.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "It [gentle parenting] is not remotely permissive," she says, putting it firmly in Baumrind's authoritative category.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Clear boundaries are "super important".
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Social media, however, is flooded with memes of exhausted parents calmly negotiating with a child having a supermarket meltdown, something Ockwell-Smith finds deeply frustrating.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "I have to step away from the Instagram reels and the TikToks because I just want to comment, 'This is not gentle parenting'".
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "You have house rules, family limits, discipline and consequences.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: But the difference is we look at discipline as learning and teaching rather than punishing." Toddler tantrums and teenage behaviour, she argues, should be viewed through a lens of ongoing brain development, not 'they're being naughty' or 'they hate me'.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: But despite the term being popular, Ockwell-Smith believes that gentle parenting is still a fringe movement and that authoritarian parenting remains the dominant style.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Around 80 years ago, American paediatrician Dr Benjamin Spock published a book called Baby and Child Care, which went on to sell millions of copies and became the main source of advice for mothers for generations.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: The opening line was "Trust yourself.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: You know more than you think..." The book challenged strict parenting norms of the time and in the following decades parents were offered more advice from an increasing range of voices.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Research into parenting has increasingly focused on the early years - from pregnancy to the age of two when the building blocks for lifelong emotional and physical health are laid down.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: For parents, that means more advice to navigate competing messages about what is best for their children.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Professor Ellie Lee, the director of the Centre for Parenting Culture Studies, has studied parenting for more than two decades, including research into mothers' confidence and uncertainty around infant feeding.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: She says a major shift occurred in the 1990s when parenting became an increasing focus of public policy.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "Politicians started to say 'Parenting's the hardest job in the world.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Children don't come with a manual.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: We need to give parents guidance.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Parents need more support.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: We need parent education'." Advice began to emerge on almost every aspect of family life, from tummy time, to feeding, to the right buggy, she explains.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Prof Lee argues that while some public health campaigns were necessary, such as advice not to put babies to sleep on their front after research into cot deaths, the growing culture of advice began to make parents paranoid.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "Dr Spock's 'trust yourself' philosophy is now a very counter-cultural piece of advice," she says.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "What we say instead is 'always seek help'," Sarah Ockwell-Smith is widely credited with coining and popularising the term 'gentle parenting' She believes this has made parents more anxious about doing things "right".
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "Some of the things that are now presented as really high stakes are not," she says, using examples like breastfeeding exclusively for six months or how much tummy time a child needs.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "It's terrible because parents become completely exhausted." Ockwell-Smith says the volume of advice can be "deafening and confusing".
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "Actually, parents should just learn themselves and go on intuition," she says.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Others point out that there is also a problem of advice being given that is altogether wrong.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Ruth Watts is a health visitor who began sharing content on social media after becoming concerned about misinformation online.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: She had seen "experts" advise parents to wean babies onto solids early, offer treatment advice for tongue tie or allergies without medical training, and tell parents to put babies in their own rooms before six months.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Many families, she argues, are working longer hours while at the same time health services are being stripped back, leaving more parents looking online for breastfeeding, behaviour and sleep support.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "We are looking for that kind of personable, conversational approach from people, rather than reading a website." Many factors shaping family life remain outside parents' control.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: A child's temperament, special educational needs, family support, finances and their own upbringing can all influence family life.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: While some say parenting hasn't got harder but expectations have, others argue that parents today are facing more complex challenges than in previous generations with growing concerns around young people's mental health.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: There are also debates around children spending more time on screens and less time outdoors, while schools are reporting increasing behavioural challenges and lower respect for rules and authority.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Prof Lee believes parental confidence is at an all-time low.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "I think parents feel very nervous about disciplining children now because they're worried about how it's going to make them feel," she argues.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: The confusion around the "right" way to parent has led some parents to turn to courses for help.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Aymara Lamche-Brennan, who has a 22-year-old daughter, four-year-old son and six-month-old daughter, signed up for a course during the summer when another mother at the school gate mentioned she was attending.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Aymara Lamche-Brennan, pictured with her three children, signed up for a Circle of Security parenting course "The flyer said 'it's the toughest job in the world' and I thought yes it is, how can you help?'" Aymara says from her home in London.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "It's not telling you how to parent.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: It's helping you think," says Jennifer Peters, a former social worker and director of the charity Connected Lives which runs courses across London, Derbyshire and Cambridgeshire.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: She says most parents want the best for their kids but they don't always know how to get there, and that guidance can be helpful.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "I don't think people need to be bombarded with information but the group experience helps you think, 'oh, it's not just me' and lets you take a step back from it all," Peters says.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Back in Dubai, Rosie says the arrival of her second child changed everything as she realised her sons were "polar opposites" and there is no one-size-fits-all solution.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: A recent trip home to Birmingham also provided some perspective.

sentences.text: Her eldest son was throwing a tantrum, and Rosie found herself wrestling with a familiar worry.

sentences.text: "If I send him upstairs, am I damaging him emotionally?
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Is he going to develop an attachment disorder because of this?" But her mum said, 'Just send him upstairs.

sentences.text: He can't hit his brother over the head with a horse [if he is upstairs].
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Follow through with your actions.' Rosie is taking this "generational advice" on board and has started "venting on social media" to show other mums that they are not alone.

sentences.text: Sir Anthony Seldon, former head teacher and author on AI in education, says the technology is being used more and more frequently, but that its introduction has been "chaotic and anarchic".
sentences.article_title: Schools not ready for AI and 'crying out' for government guidance, report warns

sentences.text: His report calls for the government to roll out a national framework for adopting AI in education in England, including training teachers on how to use it, which schools should use to develop their own "AI strategies" by September next year.
sentences.article_title: Schools not ready for AI and 'crying out' for government guidance, report warns

sentences.text: The government says its changes to the curriculum in England will give children digital skills and help them spot disinformation.
sentences.article_title: Schools not ready for AI and 'crying out' for government guidance, report warns

sentences.text: Sir Anthony's report, co-authored with venture capitalist Tim Bunting, says schools have not been prepared for AI's arrival.
sentences.article_title: Schools not ready for AI and 'crying out' for government guidance, report warns

sentences.text: Sir Anthony co-founded the group AI in Education, which was set up in 2023 to help educational institutions navigate AI safely.
sentences.article_title: Schools not ready for AI and 'crying out' for government guidance, report warns

sentences.text: His report argues that getting a grip of AI requires the same level of national urgency as wars and epidemics, and requires a taskforce modelled on the one which helped to roll out the Covid vaccine.
sentences.article_title: Schools not ready for AI and 'crying out' for government guidance, report warns

sentences.text: "Put simply, education has not kept pace with how – and how much – young people are already using AI, and that gap is starting to show up as a loss of perceived value in the institution itself," the report says.

sentences.article_title: Schools not ready for AI and 'crying out' for government guidance, report warns

sentences.article_title: Schools not ready for AI and 'crying out' for government guidance, report warns

sentences.text: Cases of antisemitism affecting university students and staff in the UK increased in the last academic year, according to a charity that monitors antisemitic incidents.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The Community Security Trust (CST) said it had recorded 95 "university-related" incidents in the 2025-26 academic year - up from 83 the year before.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: It said the number had fallen from its peak in the year after Hamas attacked Israel on 7 October 2023 and the war in Gaza began, but remains "substantially higher" than before that point.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Universities UK (UUK) represents more than 140 institutions and said its members needed to "protect Jewish students and staff", adding that the findings were a "serious concern".
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Lucy Powell, education secretary in England, said the findings in the CST report were "deeply troubling".
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: "We expect universities to take a zero-tolerance approach to antisemitism, and are providing training to help university staff identify and respond to incidents swiftly," she said.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The CST defines an antisemitic incident as "university-related" if it concerns a student, member of staff or academic at a UK university "in their academic or student capacity" - including on campus and online.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: In 2022-23, the last academic year before the 7 October attack, the CST recorded 53 incidents.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: A woman convinced her former partner she had given birth to two children who most likely did not exist in what a High Court judge described as an "extraordinary" and "elaborate campaign of deceit".
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The man, who has not been named but was referred to as John in the judgement, applied to the Family Court after he was told the woman had sold their two children for a combined £500.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The case heard that the man received messages and photos of the children and paid the woman around £30,000 over the course of two years.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: But in a hearing in February, the woman, who was referred to as Jane, told the judge she had lied about the pregnancies for revenge, claiming the man had abused her.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The court heard the man believed he was the children's' father because in late 2022 his partner told him she was pregnant, sent pictures of an ultrasound image and had become "visibly pregnant" as time went on.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: In May 2023, shortly before the first baby was due, the woman called the police alleging she had been assaulted by the man.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: He was arrested and subsequently held on remand for several months, Mrs Justice Judd said in her ruling which was published on Friday.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: Following this, the woman sent a message to his stepfather saying the baby had been born as well as sharing baby photos.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: At one stage she is said to have sent voice notes to her former partner's mother in the middle of the night with the sound of a baby crying in the background.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: Later, she told the man she was pregnant again and the baby was due in August 2024.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: However, before the due date, the couple split up and did not reconcile.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The woman would go on to tell the man's mother the baby had been born.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The woman admitted to the court she had told him she was pregnant when they were together, and afterwards, but conceded she had told a series of elaborate lies and that there were, in fact, no children.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: She argued she was menopausal at the time and could not have been pregnant and bank statements show she attended a tanning shop on the day she said she had given birth, Mrs Justice Judd said.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: In her judgement, the judge concluded that the "factors that weigh against the children genuinely existing were very strong, stronger than the factors pointing the other way".
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: She said the man was the victim of a "sustained and elaborate campaign of deceit" which also impacted his mother and closest friend.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: "Added to this, the behaviour was cruel, leading a man and his mother to believe they had children and grandchildren respectively.", the Judge said.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The judge added she was unable to conclude the woman's motive for her behaviour but said financial fraud was a "possibility"  and that the "complex mental health problems" she suffered from may have also played a part.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: Lundy Island, in the Bristol Channel off the north Devon coast, is facing closure unless it receives meaningful rainfall Famed for its puffins, the picture-perfect island of Lundy attracts birdwatchers from all over.
sentences.article_title: Puffin island on cusp of closure as it runs out of water

sentences.text: But the island is on the cusp of being evacuated as water levels drop to the lowest ever, forcing residents to take drastic measures to ensure supplies do not run out.
sentences.article_title: Puffin island on cusp of closure as it runs out of water

sentences.text: Located in the Bristol Channel off the north Devon coast, the 5km (3.1 mile) long island is not the first place you expect to be running out of water.
sentences.article_title: Puffin island on cusp of closure as it runs out of water

sentences.text: It is rich with wildlife including puffins and seals and its rugged landscape makes for breathtaking views.
sentences.article_title: Puffin island on cusp of closure as it runs out of water

sentences.text: But speak to the handful of residents here and they will tell you of the battle waged since summer to ensure the taps do not run dry.
sentences.article_title: Puffin island on cusp of closure as it runs out of water

sentences.text: Entirely self-sufficient, the National Trust-owned island relies on a combination of rainwater and boreholes drilled into the granite for supplies.
sentences.article_title: Puffin island on cusp of closure as it runs out of water

sentences.text: Severe water shortages in Lundy are not new , with islanders and visitors previously resorting to bottled water.
sentences.article_title: Puffin island on cusp of closure as it runs out of water

sentences.text: Island managing director Derek Green said closing the island would be devastating But the hottest and driest summer on record has been a "steep learning curve" for islanders, said Lundy managing director Derek Green.
sentences.article_title: Puffin island on cusp of closure as it runs out of water

sentences.text: He said there had been no significant rainfall since April and it had barely seen 20% of the typical 1.5m (4.92ft) rain it expected by this time of year.
sentences.article_title: Puffin island on cusp of closure as it runs out of water

sentences.text: Reservoir levels dropped to 13% at their lowest, forcing emergency shipments of water from the mainland to the 28 people who live on the island.
sentences.article_title: Puffin island on cusp of closure as it runs out of water

sentences.text: Water restrictions are also in place for residents and visitors.
sentences.article_title: Puffin island on cusp of closure as it runs out of water

sentences.text: Among the more extreme measures is the removal of plugs so tourists are not tempted to take a bath.
sentences.article_title: Puffin island on cusp of closure as it runs out of water

sentences.text: The island, which is managed by the Landmark Trust, is now pumping water from ponds used by wildlife to a treatment works as a "last resort".
sentences.article_title: Puffin island on cusp of closure as it runs out of water

sentences.text: "Bringing in pond water is something we've never had to do before," Green explained.
sentences.article_title: Puffin island on cusp of closure as it runs out of water

sentences.text: "It's really our last chance saloon here.
sentences.article_title: Puffin island on cusp of closure as it runs out of water

sentences.text: "Hopefully the reserve in the pond will last until it rains but because it hasn't rained in so long, this is desperate measures," he said.
sentences.article_title: Puffin island on cusp of closure as it runs out of water

sentences.text: "We've got a working farm here and the animals need water every day... so to evacuate those animals, those people and to cancel all those holidays is something that has never happened in the history of Lundy before.
sentences.article_title: Puffin island on cusp of closure as it runs out of water

sentences.text: "It would be hugely significant... we're on the cusp of having to make that decision." The island has received emergency shipments of water from the mainland since August The use of pond water led to some recovery in reservoir levels, now at 23.7% full, but Green said islanders were simply "praying for rain".
sentences.article_title: Puffin island on cusp of closure as it runs out of water

sentences.text: BBC meteorologist David Braine said there was some rain in the forecast for Lundy, but it would take weeks to top up the groundwater and reservoirs the island relied on.
sentences.article_title: Puffin island on cusp of closure as it runs out of water

sentences.text: The very dry spring and summer followed record rainfall in the later part of the winter and it was only in March when most of reservoirs in the south-west of England were full .
sentences.article_title: Puffin island on cusp of closure as it runs out of water

sentences.text: Shipments of water on passenger ferry the MS Oldenberg from north Devon began in August.
sentences.article_title: Puffin island on cusp of closure as it runs out of water

sentences.text: The first delivery to the island of about 67,000 litres had been the biggest and cost about £7,000, said Green.
sentences.article_title: Puffin island on cusp of closure as it runs out of water

sentences.text: Since then, they have shipped 4,000 litres of water three times a week, with islanders using between 9,000 litres to 11,000 litres of water a day.
sentences.article_title: Puffin island on cusp of closure as it runs out of water

sentences.text: Getting the water from the port to residents has not been an easy process as the island only has a granite track and a handful of vehicles including three 4x4s, tractors, quadbikes and a fire engine.
sentences.article_title: Puffin island on cusp of closure as it runs out of water

sentences.text: More news stories for Devon Listen to the latest news for Devon Adding to the logistical pressure, a landslip in June closed off part of the track to the tiny village at the top of the island about 400ft above sea level.
sentences.article_title: Puffin island on cusp of closure as it runs out of water

sentences.text: Green said: "We have to offload the tanks off the ship and we have to bring them up to a staging post halfway up the hill.
sentences.article_title: Puffin island on cusp of closure as it runs out of water

sentences.text: He said the island's pub, The Tavern, had closed toilets and removed bath plugs to help conserve supplies.
sentences.article_title: Puffin island on cusp of closure as it runs out of water

sentences.text: "We can't have baths... all the plugs have been removed to resist temptation," said Scantlebury.
sentences.article_title: Puffin island on cusp of closure as it runs out of water

sentences.text: "People are showering with buckets to catch the water and then using that to flush the toilets and that's saving water.
sentences.article_title: Puffin island on cusp of closure as it runs out of water

sentences.text: He said the changing climate was more "pronounced on Lundy" and islanders needed to adapt.
sentences.article_title: Puffin island on cusp of closure as it runs out of water

sentences.text: "Forecasters are predicting it will be even warmer next year," he said.
sentences.article_title: Puffin island on cusp of closure as it runs out of water

sentences.text: "We've got to learn from this and be better prepared next year in terms of increasing the reservoir here.
sentences.article_title: Puffin island on cusp of closure as it runs out of water

sentences.text: "People need to learn to use a little less water over the winter... it's a sharp learning curve for us and the wider region." Scantlebury said he was concerned for the future and it would hard to keep levels at a "reasonable level" without meaningful rain over autumn and winter.
sentences.article_title: Puffin island on cusp of closure as it runs out of water

sentences.text: "It's a trend we have to watch out for," he said.
sentences.article_title: Puffin island on cusp of closure as it runs out of water

sentences.text: Tara McEvoy-Wilding said 2026 was the year climate change hit home for islanders Assistant warden Tara McEvoy-Wilding said 2026 had been eye-opening and the "brown, sad and crispy" vegetation was a visual reminder of how dry it had been.
sentences.article_title: Puffin island on cusp of closure as it runs out of water

sentences.text: "This year feels like the real first year people have been noticing climate change," she said.
sentences.article_title: Puffin island on cusp of closure as it runs out of water

sentences.text: "For Lundy, it's going to be a challenge going forward.
sentences.article_title: Puffin island on cusp of closure as it runs out of water

sentences.text: We're going to have to be extra mindful and plan further in advance to maintain our water security." As Green looks out over the "beautiful, remote and tranquil" landscape, he is fearing for the future.
sentences.article_title: Puffin island on cusp of closure as it runs out of water

sentences.text: When it next rains, it needs to pour, he said.
sentences.article_title: Puffin island on cusp of closure as it runs out of water

sentences.text: "I never ever thought we would have to take water from our ponds but this is the position we find ourselves in," he said.
sentences.article_title: Puffin island on cusp of closure as it runs out of water

sentences.text: "We're in real jeopardy right now unless it rains very, very soon." Follow BBC Devon on X , external , Facebook , external and Instagram , external .

sentences.text: The Nasa-led team of scientists took samples of ancient rock from the north-west Highlands Nasa scientists are studying rocks in the Scottish Highlands to help them understand if there was once life on Mars.
sentences.article_title: Nasa heads to Scottish Highlands in its search for life on Mars

sentences.text: The US space agency announced last year that its Perseverance rover had found potential biosignatures , markings on rocks possibly made by ancient microbes.
sentences.article_title: Nasa heads to Scottish Highlands in its search for life on Mars

sentences.text: This summer, scientists took samples from a geological feature called the Stoer Formation , external around Clachtoll, in Assynt, in the north-west Highlands.
sentences.article_title: Nasa heads to Scottish Highlands in its search for life on Mars

sentences.text: Nasa said the area's rocks formed in environments comparable to ancient Martian lakes and rivers, but could also hold evidence of microbial life from 1.2 billion years ago.
sentences.article_title: Nasa heads to Scottish Highlands in its search for life on Mars

sentences.text: Scientists surveying rocks at Clachtoll in Assynt earlier this year Perseverance, shown in a concept image, has detected potential biosignatures Clachtoll is a small crofting community on the Sutherland coast about 100 miles north of Inverness, and is a popular destination along the North Coast 500 tourist route.
sentences.article_title: Nasa heads to Scottish Highlands in its search for life on Mars

sentences.text: Nasa's Goddard Instrument Field Team, which specialises in studying Earth's extreme environments, led the research expedition.
sentences.article_title: Nasa heads to Scottish Highlands in its search for life on Mars

sentences.text: Experts from the universities of Glasgow and Cambridge were among those involved.
sentences.article_title: Nasa heads to Scottish Highlands in its search for life on Mars

sentences.text: They took rock samples from cliffs for further analysis.
sentences.article_title: Nasa heads to Scottish Highlands in its search for life on Mars

sentences.text: Nasa said: "Though Mars is dry today, the Martian landscape, like our own planet's, is shaped by an ancient history of flowing water.
sentences.article_title: Nasa heads to Scottish Highlands in its search for life on Mars

sentences.text: "Both worlds have layered areas of mudstones and siltstones rich in clay minerals.
sentences.article_title: Nasa heads to Scottish Highlands in its search for life on Mars

sentences.text: Last year, technology which will be used in the search for evidence of Martian life was tested by a University of St Andrews team at Lower Diabaig, in Torridon.
sentences.article_title: Nasa heads to Scottish Highlands in its search for life on Mars

sentences.text: The rocks in the area are billions of years old and similar to those found on the Red Planet.
sentences.article_title: Nasa heads to Scottish Highlands in its search for life on Mars

sentences.text: Eight years ago, a Nasa Mars rover, Curiosity, explored a part of the planet named after Torridon .
sentences.article_title: Nasa heads to Scottish Highlands in its search for life on Mars

sentences.text: Martian geological areas and features have been named by Nasa after places on Earth.
sentences.article_title: Nasa heads to Scottish Highlands in its search for life on Mars

sentences.text: Several of the names were taken from Scotland and, as well as Torridon, there is a Siccar Point, Muck, Wick, Sandwick and Holyrood on Mars.
sentences.article_title: Nasa heads to Scottish Highlands in its search for life on Mars

sentences.text: Nasa chose the name Torridon due to the Torridonian Supergroup, a geological formation in the north-west Highlands that contains some of the oldest evidence of life of any rocks in the UK.
sentences.article_title: Nasa heads to Scottish Highlands in its search for life on Mars

sentences.text: This video can not be played Aviva boss says it 'doesn't make sense' to be building homes in flood zones as risk increases Homes are being built today that could become uninsurable in the future due to the risk of flooding, the boss of insurance giant Aviva has said.
sentences.article_title: Warning more homes will be uninsurable due to flood risk

sentences.text: Amanda Blanc said the risk of flooding is "absolutely increasing", but based on current building patterns 115,000 new homes will be built in flood zones in the next decade.
sentences.article_title: Warning more homes will be uninsurable due to flood risk

sentences.text: "That doesn't seem to me to make sense.
sentences.article_title: Warning more homes will be uninsurable due to flood risk

sentences.text: We need to think about where those homes are being built," she told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Warning more homes will be uninsurable due to flood risk

sentences.text: About 6.3 million homes and businesses in England are at risk of flooding, according to the Environment Agency, and Aviva research found one in nine homes built between 2022 and 2024 are at medium to high risk of flooding.
sentences.article_title: Warning more homes will be uninsurable due to flood risk

sentences.text: Blanc told the BBC's Big Boss Interview podcast that England was "for sure" building homes that might be uninsurable at some point in the future.
sentences.article_title: Warning more homes will be uninsurable due to flood risk

sentences.text: "It's very well known where these flooding areas are.
sentences.article_title: Warning more homes will be uninsurable due to flood risk

sentences.text: Let's think very carefully about homes that are being built." Blanc said construction that borders those flood zones also needs a different approach.
sentences.article_title: Warning more homes will be uninsurable due to flood risk

sentences.text: "You can do all sorts of different things to your property to make it more or less vulnerable to flood," she said.
sentences.article_title: Warning more homes will be uninsurable due to flood risk

sentences.text: According to Aviva's research, nearly a third of new homes built in 2024 will be at risk of some flooding by 2050, and one in seven would be at medium to high risk of flooding as extreme weather becomes more acute.
sentences.article_title: Warning more homes will be uninsurable due to flood risk

sentences.text: Earlier this year the Met Office estimated that with current levels of global warming, record-breaking wet winters like the one experienced in the UK in 2023-24 have gone from once in 80-year events to once in 20-year events .
sentences.article_title: Warning more homes will be uninsurable due to flood risk

sentences.text: A spokesperson for the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs said: "We've put a record amount of investment into protecting nearly 900,000 properties against billions of pounds of flooding damage.
sentences.article_title: Warning more homes will be uninsurable due to flood risk

sentences.text: Aviva is a major UK private pension provider, and Blanc said speculation over the last couple of Budgets about changes to pensions led to a significant increase in withdrawals.
sentences.article_title: Warning more homes will be uninsurable due to flood risk

sentences.text: "Effectively we saw in the last year 30 times the normal withdrawal from pensions that we would normally see, which is clearly something which customers may regret afterwards because once you take your tax-free lump sum out, you can't put it back in," she said.
sentences.article_title: Warning more homes will be uninsurable due to flood risk

sentences.text: "So we would say be very, very thoughtful about the things that you are testing, thinking about." The few policy announcements ahead of the Budget so far have included a scheme to help first-time buyers get on to the property ladder , and a commitment from Healey to deliver a "new age of industrialisation" for the UK.
sentences.article_title: Warning more homes will be uninsurable due to flood risk

sentences.text: Healey has said previously that Budget speculation is unhelpful as it has a "direct impact on the decisions that investors hold back from, or may make".
sentences.article_title: Warning more homes will be uninsurable due to flood risk

sentences.text: A Treasury spokesperson said: "The chancellor makes tax policy decisions at fiscal events.
sentences.article_title: Warning more homes will be uninsurable due to flood risk

sentences.text: Blanc said Aviva was "ready with capital" to invest in infrastructure, pointing out that the company already invests more than £100bn in the UK, £35bn of which goes into infrastructure, from hospitals to schools to windfarms.
sentences.article_title: Warning more homes will be uninsurable due to flood risk

sentences.text: We want to invest, we're a big UK employer.
sentences.article_title: Warning more homes will be uninsurable due to flood risk

sentences.text: We want to invest in UK infrastructure.
sentences.article_title: Warning more homes will be uninsurable due to flood risk

sentences.text: It provides good returns for our pension holders and for the members of those pension schemes," she said, but added detail was needed to turn it into reality.
sentences.article_title: Warning more homes will be uninsurable due to flood risk

sentences.text: Asked about the current debate about the pension triple lock , which means the state pension rises by the highest of either average wage increases, inflation or 2.5%, and whether the government is looking to change that, Blanc said it was not for her to say what should happen.
sentences.article_title: Warning more homes will be uninsurable due to flood risk

sentences.text: But potential lower annual increases to pensions if the triple lock is changed would have knock-on effects, she added.
sentences.article_title: Warning more homes will be uninsurable due to flood risk

sentences.text: "If you've got a lower state pension then you need a higher private pension, don't you?
sentences.article_title: Warning more homes will be uninsurable due to flood risk

sentences.text: So you need to think about that balance," Blanc said.

sentences.article_title: Sheff Utd expect to avoid points deduction - CEO

sentences.text: Blades chief executive officer Stephen Bettis spent an hour in the BBC Radio Sheffield studio on Tuesday night , with the potential points deduction top of the agenda.
sentences.article_title: Sheff Utd expect to avoid points deduction - CEO

sentences.text: Bettis said: "The EFL are investigating the process and what has happened.
sentences.article_title: Sheff Utd expect to avoid points deduction - CEO

sentences.text: "The 12-point deduction only relates to if the club or a company within the group goes into insolvency.
sentences.article_title: Sheff Utd expect to avoid points deduction - CEO

sentences.text: The advice our owners have got from their lawyers is that the club certainly didn't go into insolvency - we're funded, we're paying all our bills on time.
sentences.article_title: Sheff Utd expect to avoid points deduction - CEO

sentences.text: "The company that no longer is in the group has now had a winding up order against it.
sentences.article_title: Sheff Utd expect to avoid points deduction - CEO

sentences.text: "The position of our owners is that the winding up petition happened after that entity was no longer within the Sheffield United group.
sentences.article_title: Sheff Utd expect to avoid points deduction - CEO

sentences.text: While it was within the group it never had a winding up order, it didn't become insolvent - their belief is that that stops the 12-point deduction happening." BBC Sport has contacted the EFL for comment.
sentences.article_title: Sheff Utd expect to avoid points deduction - CEO

sentences.text: Though not a direct comparison, in 2009 Southampton were docked 10 points by the EFL after their parent company went into administration and the football club claimed there was not a financial link between the two.
sentences.article_title: Sheff Utd expect to avoid points deduction - CEO

sentences.text: Bettis added: "It wasn't a parent company for Sheffield United when it happened, that's quite an important difference.
sentences.article_title: Sheff Utd expect to avoid points deduction - CEO

sentences.text: "The EFL have been aware of this for four months, if it was clear cut we'd have been charged already, in my opinion.
sentences.article_title: Sheff Utd expect to avoid points deduction - CEO

sentences.text: It's clearly not clear cut and it continues to go on.
sentences.article_title: Sheff Utd expect to avoid points deduction - CEO

sentences.text: "The owners have cooperated fully with the EFL investigation.
sentences.article_title: Sheff Utd expect to avoid points deduction - CEO

sentences.text: They are now deliberating internally and we're waiting for their response." Asked by BBC Radio Sheffield's Rob Staton if that means the club are not expecting a points deduction, Bettis said: "From the advice the lawyers for our owners were given - that is what we've been told.
sentences.article_title: Sheff Utd expect to avoid points deduction - CEO

sentences.text: "I'm not going to sit here and categorically say we're not at risk, until the verdict is given I'm not going to make myself look an idiot.
sentences.article_title: Sheff Utd expect to avoid points deduction - CEO

sentences.article_title: Sheff Utd expect to avoid points deduction - CEO

sentences.text: Those discussions continue," he said.

sentences.text: Ghana is a predominantly Christian country where preaching on public transport is widespread.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: On long-distance buses, pastors can often be seen - and heard - preaching the gospel.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: The faithful sometimes offer money to the preachers to support their endeavours.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: But a new law means this familiar practice could be coming to an end.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: Anyone found preaching in public service vehicles faces up to eight months in prison, a fine of up to $52 (£39) or both.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: The new regulation, passed by parliament in May, and which has started to be enforced in recent weeks, targets preaching and hawking on vehicles while they are in motion, classifying both as a nuisance and citing the safety and comfort of passengers.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: Boateng, a 61-year-old pastor at Gospel Light church, has been preaching on commercial vehicles leaving Neoplan station since 2023.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: "I preach on commercial vehicles because not everyone is able to go to church on Sunday.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: There are a lot of passengers who need our message of salvation to repent from their sins.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: We even heal the sick on some buses," he told the BBC in Twi, a local language.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: Wearing a clerical collared shirt, Boateng moves through rows of buses loading passengers before boarding one bound for Kumasi, Ghana's second-largest city.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: We speak to him before the bus departs to avoid breaking the law.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: Some travellers listen closely as he delivers his message.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: Others try to ignore him, browsing their phones, making calls or chatting among themselves.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: "Some passengers are very happy with my message.
sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: Critics say preaching on moving vehicles is a nuisance and a safety risk, as it could distract the driver, while supporters argue that evangelism is a Christian duty and should be protected under the freedom of religious worship.

sentences.text: Some of them spit saliva on you unconsciously, especially if you are seated not far from them, and they are a nuisance in terms of noise and saliva.

sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.article_title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer

sentences.text: Seven countries have expressed interest in hosting the 2036 Olympics The International Olympic Committee (IOC) has confirmed South Africa have shown an interest in becoming the first African host of the summer Olympics in 2036.

sentences.text: The discovery of the bodies of 12 women over three months, in the city of Ekurhuleni, near Johannesburg has reignited questions about the scale of what many people see as being a crisis of violence against women.

sentences.text: The country has one of the highest murder rates in the world, with 5,427 people murdered between April and June this year alone.

sentences.text: In that period, according to the South African Human Rights Commission, 569 women were killed, an average of six a day, and 1,052 others survived attempted murder.

sentences.text: A report in 2022 by the Human Sciences Research Council found that more than 35% of South African women experienced physical or sexual violence, many from their own intimate partners.

sentences.text: The latest measures announced by Ramaphosa, including better street lighting and a review of unsolved cases , are too little, he says, and too late.

sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: The new monarch has long been a familiar face in the East African nation, where for many he was known not as the heir to the throne, but as a storyteller: a long-serving anchor and editor at the state broadcaster.

sentences.text: But the 56-year-old - now King Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma Nyabongo I - has become the subject of media attention himself as his rise to the Tooro throne sparked controversy and widespread reactions beyond the country.

sentences.text: Tooro is one of Uganda's four main officially recognised historical kingdoms.
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: For the last 31 years, it had been headed by King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV, who was once known as a "boy king", after ascending to the throne as an infant.

sentences.text: Oyo became king in 1995 at the age of just three, following the death of his father.
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: Kijanangoma has had to perform various ceremonies and walk about 4km (2.5 miles) to the official Karuziika royal palace where he has now been crowned.
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: The Tooro kingdom's Information Minister Charles Mwanguhya told the BBC Focus on Africa podcast that a mock fight would follow his crowning, to signify that kingship does not come easy.

sentences.text: Kijanangoma would then be blessed by members of the royal Babiito clan, he said.
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: According to tradition, a recognised son of the late king should have succeeded him.
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: Close members of the royal family said Oyo had left a young son and a will with instructions that the child should be next on the throne.
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: But the son has never been revealed to the public and nor was he recognised by the committee of 21 Babiito clan members who choose the king and eventually selected Kijanangoma.
sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.article_title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: Magicians, jugglers, puppeteers and acrobats once made a living from crowds in public spaces.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: Changing entertainment habits and tighter restrictions have made audiences harder to find, pushing many out of the profession.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: Khan, one of India's best-known magicians, comes from the Madari community, which has a long tradition of performing in public spaces.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: There are no official figures, but Khan says community records identify about 400 Madari families in Delhi, with hundreds more in Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan and Telangana.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: Despite their small numbers today, the Madaris trace their roots back centuries.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: Historian Ashok Mathur says Madari traditions have roots in Indian folklore, mythology and the long history of travelling performers.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: "For generations, these skills were passed through families," he explains.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: Restricted access to community spaces has made it difficult for street magicians to find an audience Khan followed the same path, learning magic from his father and uncles and performing from the age of 12.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: By his early 20s, he had mastered the rope trick that would later make him famous.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: The trick – in which a rope appears to rise into the air before a boy climbs it – was long associated with the mythology of Indian street magic and widely considered impossible, until Khan performed it.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: He says it took six years to master the trick, which he first performed publicly in 1995 outside Delhi's iconic Qutub Minar.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: Two years later, he performed it before 30,000 people on a beach in Karnataka.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: His trick brought international attention,  and that led to tours to the UK, France, Germany and Japan.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: Khan hoped the fame would shine a light on India's traditional performers.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: As audiences turned to new forms of entertainment and public performance opportunities dwindled, many magicians found it harder to make a living from skills passed down through generations.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: One of them is 40-year-old Imam Khan.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: Once a magician, Imam now makes a living collecting bottles and recyclables from Delhi's streets.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: He spends much of his time rag-picking near a western Delhi dump, earning about 200 rupees ($2; £1.57) a day.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: Experts say the decline in street performance has multiple causes, chief among them the changing nature of public spaces.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: An old picture of Khan performing the great rope trick Anurupa Roy, founder of Katkatha Puppet Arts Trust, says performers increasingly struggle to find audiences as public spaces shrink.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: "Closed parks and residential societies that bar outsiders are limiting spaces for performance." Researcher and performer Komita Dhanda says changing attitudes to public spaces are also driving the decline.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: "With tighter security, especially in busy town and city centres, there is little space left for street performers," she says.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: It is not just individual artists who struggle to get permission.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: Dhanda says her well-known street theatre group, Jana Natya Manch, often faces hurdles performing in public spaces.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: For many artists, the challenge is not just finding a venue but navigating unclear rules over what is allowed.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: Most street performers rely on voluntary payments, but experts say the line between performing for money and begging can blur.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: Unlike the UK, India has no federal busking framework.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: Performers instead navigate state-level rules on public order, obstruction, noise and public land.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: "This is why street performers often have to face municipal and police regulations governing public spaces, as well as state-specific anti-begging laws," says lawyer Kaushik Mitra.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: Imam Khan has left street performance behind and now makes a living as a ragpicker For many artists, Covid made a bad situation worse.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: When India imposed its 2020 lockdown, public performances stopped.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: Many magicians returned to their villages; some never came back.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: "We saw a decline in public performances after this period," Dhanda says.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: "The brunt was especially harsh for street magicians and performers, many of whom did not return to cities." For the artists who did return and continue the trade, the challenges only increased.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: Shahim Khan, 42, still performs magic on Delhi's streets, sometimes with his 12-year-old daughter, Alia.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: Much of his work is now confined to industrial areas, far from the busy public spaces where he once performed, hitting his earnings hard.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: Before the pandemic, he could stage four or five shows a day, earning 1,000-1,200 rupees.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: "Now I barely manage two shows and earn 200-400 rupees," he says.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: The rise of short-form digital entertainment has added to the pressures on traditional performers, experts say.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: So have changing attitudes towards street arts.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: "There was a lot of Western interest in things like the rope trick decades ago.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: But forms and tastes have changed, and so has what India chooses to showcase," Dhanda says.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: For Khan, the loss is about more than money.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: He fears an art passed down generations could disappear if no-one learns it.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: "A trick can survive only if someone learns it," he says.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: His son, Altamash, began performing with him as a teenager but now works decorating parties with balloons.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: In his 30s, he has largely left performing behind.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: Years without regular practice have dulled his skills.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: When he demonstrated his juggling for the BBC, he struggled to find the rhythm.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: "I am slowly forgetting all the tricks," he said.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: Khan had hoped his son would carry on the family tradition.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: Altamash had hoped to make a name for himself too, but it did not work out.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: "I knew I may not achieve the fame my father has, but I did not think there would come a time when performing would not remain an option," he says.
sentences.article_title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians

sentences.text: Karl Bushby is one step closer to his journey's end after reaching the UK Adventurer Karl Bushby says he has completed a multi-day swim of the English Channel, stepping foot on UK soil after a 28-year journey.
sentences.article_title: Karl Bushby completes English Channel swim

sentences.text: Bushby, 57, left Chile, South America, on 1 November 1998, following two self-imposed rules - not to use transport to advance and not to return home until the journey is complete.
sentences.article_title: Karl Bushby completes English Channel swim

sentences.text: On Tuesday, he announced that he had swum from France to the UK - the final, major hurdle of his journey back to his childhood home in Hull.
sentences.article_title: Karl Bushby completes English Channel swim

sentences.text: Bushby said: "[It] feels good to have UK soil under my feet after all these years.
sentences.article_title: Karl Bushby completes English Channel swim

sentences.text: HM Coastguard said it "liaised with French authorities and maritime sector partners to ensure safety protocols were met".
sentences.article_title: Karl Bushby completes English Channel swim

sentences.text: Bushby's team said he was welcomed on the beach by a small gathering of friends and family, including his father, Keith Bushby, a former SAS soldier, and acclaimed filmmaker Werner Herzog, who is directing a feature-length documentary about the journey titled Walk of Life.
sentences.article_title: Karl Bushby completes English Channel swim

sentences.text: For many years, the French have only tolerated cross channel swims departing from the UK - not from France.
sentences.article_title: Karl Bushby completes English Channel swim

sentences.text: However, Bushby's team said permission had been sought from both French and UK authorities, and said they chose not to publicise exactly when it would take place "for safety and security reasons".
sentences.article_title: Karl Bushby completes English Channel swim

sentences.text: Bushby steps foot on Shakespeare beach near Dover in Kent To date, Bushby has covered more than 30,000 miles (48,000km), including 29 countries.
sentences.article_title: Karl Bushby completes English Channel swim

sentences.text: He walked the length of South America, crossed the treacherous Darien Gap and continued north to Alaska.
sentences.article_title: Karl Bushby completes English Channel swim

sentences.text: From there he crossed the Bering Strait on foot, swimming where necessary.
sentences.article_title: Karl Bushby completes English Channel swim

sentences.text: Karl battling through ice as he crosses the Bering Strait to cross into Russia in 2006 Bushby then traversed Siberia and the rest of Asia before swimming across the Caspian Sea, which took 31 days to complete.
sentences.article_title: Karl Bushby completes English Channel swim

sentences.text: He crossed into Europe last year and arrived at the English Channel last month.
sentences.article_title: Karl Bushby completes English Channel swim

sentences.text: The journey has been dogged by problems, with visa restrictions, the 2008 financial crash which cost him sponsors, Covid-19 and geopolitics having all stopped him in his tracks.
sentences.article_title: Karl Bushby completes English Channel swim

sentences.text: In June, Channel Tunnel bosses vetoed his request for access to a service tunnel , which he said left him with no other option than to swim.
sentences.article_title: Karl Bushby completes English Channel swim

sentences.text: In September, when the BBC met Bushby in Belgium, he said how he felt it was "definitely time to call it a day", adding: "I don't want to keep this going for much longer." He said he had always been fascinated with nature and horizons, which fuelled his thirst for adventure.
sentences.article_title: Karl Bushby completes English Channel swim

sentences.text: It is expected he will reach Hull by early November.
sentences.article_title: Karl Bushby completes English Channel swim

sentences.text: Listen to highlights from Hull and East Yorkshire on BBC Sounds , and watch the latest episode of Look North .
sentences.article_title: Karl Bushby completes English Channel swim

sentences.text: Daniel Kinahan, shown here in a court artist's sketch, appeared in court by videolink from prison A solicitor from Northern Ireland is to represent suspected mob boss Daniel Kinahan before the Irish courts in Dublin.
sentences.article_title: Belfast solicitor to represent suspected mob boss Kinahan

sentences.text: A defence barrister David Perry told the Special Criminal Court on Monday that Darragh Mackin would be Kinahan's defence solicitor.
sentences.article_title: Belfast solicitor to represent suspected mob boss Kinahan

sentences.text: Kinahan, 49, appeared before court by videolink from Portlaoise Prison for the second time as he faces a charge of directing the activities of a criminal organisation.
sentences.article_title: Belfast solicitor to represent suspected mob boss Kinahan

sentences.text: During his first court appearance last August, he did not have any legal representation.
sentences.article_title: Belfast solicitor to represent suspected mob boss Kinahan

sentences.text: Mackin, from Phoenix Law in Belfast, was unable to appear in court in Dublin on Monday as he was attending "other matters elsewhere", which were "unexpected", Perry told the court.
sentences.article_title: Belfast solicitor to represent suspected mob boss Kinahan

sentences.text: Perry asked if the matter could be pushed back for a week and Judge Caroline Biggs remanded the matter for seven days.
sentences.article_title: Belfast solicitor to represent suspected mob boss Kinahan

sentences.text: Perry said Kinahan would appear in person at the next court appearance next Monday, adding that it was his preference to appear in person.
sentences.article_title: Belfast solicitor to represent suspected mob boss Kinahan

sentences.text: Kinahan was extradited from the United Arab Emirates (UAE) on 9 August and flew back to Ireland on board the Irish government's new jet.
sentences.article_title: Belfast solicitor to represent suspected mob boss Kinahan

sentences.text: He was brought before the Special Criminal Court in Dublin in a high security operation and charged with directing the activities of a criminal organisation between 18 October 2015 and 6 April 2017.
sentences.article_title: Belfast solicitor to represent suspected mob boss Kinahan

sentences.text: Kinahan was arrested in the UAE in April.
sentences.article_title: Belfast solicitor to represent suspected mob boss Kinahan

sentences.text: He appealed the extradition order over the past few months but his attempts were unsuccessful.
sentences.article_title: Belfast solicitor to represent suspected mob boss Kinahan

sentences.text: The UK's National Crime Agency (NCA) has previously said that the Kinahan cartel has been responsible for importing tonnes of drugs and firearms around the world and has also been linked to more than a dozen gangland murders.
sentences.article_title: Belfast solicitor to represent suspected mob boss Kinahan

sentences.text: Kinahan was not only wanted by the authorities in Ireland - the US Treasury Department once described the Kinahan cartel as one of the most dangerous in the world.
sentences.article_title: Belfast solicitor to represent suspected mob boss Kinahan

sentences.text: Kinahan faces the charge before the Special Criminal Court, which is a three-judge, non-jury court.
